places.name: Aguinaldo Shrine (Museo ni Emilio Aguinaldo)
places.description: Stand where the Philippines was born! On June 12, 1898, Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed independence from the window and balcony of this grand house in Kawit, and the national flag was first officially raised here. Today the mansion is a free museum run by the NHCP. Tour the grand hall, conference room and azotea, peek at the hidden compartments, secret doors and escape tunnel that Aguinaldo designed, and see the ground-floor exhibits on Cavite's role in the Revolution. Then stroll the park out front for the classic balcony photo. Come on a weekday morning, since the museum closes on Mondays and gets busy with school trips and around Independence Day.
places.best_time_to_visit: Tuesday to Friday mornings; June 12 for the national Independence Day rites (expect crowds and security).

places.name: Aguinid Falls
places.description: You don't just look at this waterfall, you climb it! Aguinid Falls in Tangbo, Samboan stacks level after level along the Tangbo River, each with its own cascade. With a trained local guide, you scramble up smooth limestone walls, swim in turquoise basins and slide down where it's safe. It's an adventurous, less crowded alternative to Kawasan and an easy add-on to an Oslob day. Wear aqua shoes, leave valuables behind and go in the morning before the crowds. Samboan has at least 12 waterfalls, so ask about Dau Falls if you still have energy. Bring a dry bag and plenty of water.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry-season mornings

places.name: Alegria Falls (Kanlaob and Cancalanog)
places.description: Cebu's ice-cold, turquoise alternative to the Kawasan crowds! Alegria has two falls that make a perfect day together. Kanlaob Falls sits right off a paved road, so you can jump into its blue-green pool with no trek at all. Cancalanog Falls is a short, steep walk down into a mossy gorge, with deep pools for cliff jumping and a little bamboo bridge over the water. Each one costs just ₱50. Come at noon when the sun warms the water, and bring a towel because it is freezing at first!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, December to May; swim from noon to early afternoon when the sun is strongest. Skip it right after heavy rain.

places.name: Alibijaban Island
places.description: Alibijaban is the slow, off-grid island escape at the tip of the Bondoc Peninsula! A short boat ride from San Andres Port drops you on a white sand shore with clear, shallow water and a wide mangrove forest behind it. Lounge on a floating cottage, swim and snorkel in the calm channel, walk out to the sandbar, and ride a boat through the mangroves. Sleep in a nipa hut or a tent, then catch the soft sunrise before the island warms up. It is a long trip from Manila, so make it an overnight stay. Buy food, water and supplies in San Andres before you cross, since the island has only basic stores and limited power.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late December to early April for dry weather and calmer seas; cross in the early morning.

places.name: Alicia Panoramic Park
places.description: Bohol's other famous hills, and a sunrise you won't forget! Alicia Panoramic Park, also called the City of Clouds, is a rolling grass ridge in eastern Bohol. On clear mornings from November to March, a sea of clouds can fill the valley below while you stand above it. Hike up with a local guide before dawn, or come for a fiery sunset over the ridges. Bring a light, water and a jacket, and leave nothing but footprints!
places.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise, roughly 5:30 to 7 AM; November to March for the best chance of a sea of clouds.

places.name: Aliw Falls
places.description: A wide, roaring curtain of white water! Aliw Falls tumbles down a rocky ledge in a broad, multi-tiered cascade, and you can watch it from a wooden deck right at the plunge pool. The newer route through Pilgrim's Dream Ecofarm is a paved 20-minute walk, and the resort added turquoise pools right beside the falls. Come after a few rainy days for the biggest flow, then pair it with nearby Hulugan Falls!
places.best_time_to_visit: Late in the year, after the rains, for full falls; the falls can almost dry up by April and May.

places.name: Alona Beach
places.description: Powdery white sand, clear water and a full strip of restaurants, dive shops and bars: Alona Beach is the easy, lively base for most Bohol trips. Swim and snorkel by day, book island hopping to Balicasag and Pamilacan, or get certified at one of the many dive shops. At sunset, grab a table on the sand for grilled seafood and a cold drink, then catch some live acoustic music. It can get crowded, but the convenience is hard to beat. Best from November to May, when the sea is calm and the skies are clear.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May; sunset for dinner

opening_hours.note: Public beach; no entrance fee listed by the Panglao tourism office

places.name: Ampere Beach and Rock Formations
places.description: This is a beach for looking, not swimming, and wow, what a look! Ampere Beach, about 20 km from Baler, is covered in smooth pebbles and big boulders polished by Pacific waves, with a dramatic sea stack standing just offshore and green cliffs behind. Pull over on the coastal road, listen to the stones rattle as the waves pull back, and shoot the rock formations at sunrise. Swimming is not safe here because of strong currents and the rocky ground, so enjoy it from the shore!
places.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise or early morning on clear days; dry season for calmer seas.

places.name: Anawangin Cove
places.description: Camp under 'pine' trees by the sea! Anawangin Cove looks like nowhere else in the country: a crescent of ash-gray volcanic sand backed by agoho trees and grassy mountains, with Mt. Pinatubo in the distance. A boat ride from Pundaquit gets you there, and most groups stay overnight: pitch a tent under the trees, swim, watch the sunset, then stargaze by the campfire. Facilities are basic, so bring your own food, water and gear and take your trash home. Go in the dry season and combine it with Capones Island and Nagsasa Cove.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May dry season

places.name: Anilao (Diving and Snorkeling)
places.description: One of the world's best macro dive spots, just about 2.5 hours from Manila! Anilao in Mabini, Batangas faces Balayan Bay at the edge of the Verde Island Passage, known as the 'center of the center' of marine shore fish biodiversity. Divers come for nudibranchs, frogfish and colorful reefs; non-divers can snorkel, try an intro dive or island-hop to spots like Sombrero Island. Dive resorts line the coast. Make it a weekend: dive or snorkel by day, then chill with a sunset view of the bay.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May for calmer seas; March to May is peak, so book early

places.name: Antong Falls
places.description: Nine layers of waterfalls tumbling through a bouldery river into deep turquoise pools! Antong Falls in Inmalog, Sison, is a series of cascades mostly 1 to 6 meters high, with the tallest, about 20 meters, hidden upstream where it pours against a cave. Trek at least 30 minutes from the trailhead, swim in the pools and jump from the first level if the water is deep enough. Go with a local guide from the barangay, and start early to beat the heat and the afternoon rain!
places.best_time_to_visit: Just after the rainy season for strong flow, or dry months for clearer, calmer water. Start early in the morning.

places.name: Apo Island
places.description: Swim with sea turtles! Apo Island is a small island off southern Negros and one of the world's best-known community-run marine sanctuaries. In 1982, the community, helped by Silliman University marine biologist Angel Alcala, protected part of its reef, and it paid off: as many as 385 fish species live here, plus green and hawksbill turtles. Snorkel off the beach and you'll likely float beside turtles grazing on seagrass. Boats leave Malatapay for the crossing of about 30-45 minutes. Go early, since boats head back by mid-afternoon.
places.best_time_to_visit: Calm-sea months, March to June; mornings

places.name: Apo Reef Natural Park
places.description: Apo Reef is the Philippines' largest coral reef system and the big-league dive and snorkel trip of Mindoro. Sablayan's bangkas cross to Apo Island, a palm-shaded islet with a century-old mangrove lagoon and a lighthouse, then drop you over walls and coral gardens where sharks, turtles, stingrays, mantas and big schools of jacks hang out. Snorkel the shallows, dive the walls, climb to the lighthouse and camp overnight under a sky full of stars. It is an ASEAN Heritage Park, and since 2026 the marine heart of Sablayan's UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Book the boat and permit with the Sablayan Tourism Office at least three working days ahead, and go between March and early June for the calmest seas.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to mid-June; calmest and clearest March to early June. Crossings are suspended in rough habagat swell (roughly late June to October). Boats leave Sablayan at first light.

places.name: Aqua Planet
places.description: Aqua Planet is the big one: a 10-hectare water park inside Clark Freeport with more than 38 slides and attractions, billed as the largest in the country! Thrill seekers line up for the Aqua Loop, where a trap door drops you into a 360-degree loop, then the four-person Tornado funnel and the Super Bowl. Need a breather? Float the 412-meter Wave River, ride the waves in the 3,500-square-meter wave pool, or try the Flow Ride surf machine. Little ones get their own splash zone with a tipping bucket. Arrive at opening and hit the big slides first, wear proper swimwear (no cotton), and load your Planet Band wristband, because the park is cashless with no re-entry.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekdays, right at opening (10 AM), before the midday crowd builds. Summer (March to May) is peak season. Rides may pause in thunderstorms.

places.name: Ariel's Point
places.description: Ready to jump? Ariel's Point is Boracay's favorite adventure day trip, a rocky cove on the Buruanga coast with cliff-diving platforms at 5, 8 and 15 metres. A boat leaves from Station 1, and once there you can jump, kayak, paddleboard, snorkel or hike the nature trail. Not into jumping? Cheering from the deck counts too. The ticket covers a buffet lunch, snacks, unlimited drinks including cocktails and beer, and an afternoon dessert, which makes it a classic group day out. Best moment: watching your friends take the 15-metre leap, then cruising back to Boracay in time for sunset.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May for calm seas

places.name: Art in Island
places.description: No 'do not touch' signs here: you are part of the art! Art in Island in Cubao is a two-storey, 3,800-square-meter 3D art museum where optical-illusion murals become scenes you climb into, ride or run from once you pose and snap. It opened in November 2014, with its first murals painted by 18 Korean visual artists, and it is one of the largest 3D art museums in Asia, with around 100 interactive artworks, including fun takes on the Mona Lisa and The Scream. Bring friends who will take turns behind the camera, charge your phone and wear colors that pop. A sure win on rainy days.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday afternoons for shorter photo queues, or any rainy day.

places.name: Ayala Museum
places.description: Sixty tiny worlds that tell the whole Philippine story: the Ayala Museum dioramas are worth seeing at least once! Envisioned by painter Fernando Zobel and opened in 1967, the museum at Greenbelt reopened in December 2021 after a big renovation by Leandro V. Locsin Partners. Walk past 60 handcrafted history dioramas, then step into Gold of Ancestors, with more than 1,000 precolonial gold objects that will leave you in awe. Add the textile, ceramics and changing art exhibits for a full afternoon. It is air-conditioned and compact, a good pick for a rainy-day date or a family trip, with Greenbelt food steps away.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday afternoons, or any rainy day.

places.name: Ayala Triangle Gardens
places.description: Makati's favorite green breather, right in the middle of the office towers! Ayala Triangle Gardens sits on land that used to be Nielson Field, Manila's prewar airport, and Ayala Avenue and Paseo de Roxas follow its old runways. Today it has big shady trees, lawns and public art, plus restaurants around the edge, including two-Michelin-star Helm and Blackbird in the old Nielson Tower. Come for a morning jog, an after-work snack date or a chill walk with friends. At Christmas, lights fill the trees and the gardens host shows and markets. Late afternoon to early evening is the sweet spot.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to evening; November to early January for the Christmas lights.

places.name: Baclayon Church
places.description: This is where Christianity took root in Bohol! Jesuit missionaries founded Baclayon in 1596, and its coral-stone church was completed in 1727. The 2013 earthquake brought down its portico and bell tower, but after more than four years of careful restoration it reopened in 2018, and it is a top stop for history lovers. Step inside to see the restored retablos, then visit the convent museum with centuries-old vestments and religious art. It is a short ride from Tagbilaran, so it fits perfectly as the first stop of a countryside tour. Go in the morning when it is cooler and before tour groups arrive.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning, before tour groups arrive.

places.name: Badian Canyoneering
places.description: Cebu's top group adventure! Badian canyoneering means strapping on a helmet and life vest, then trekking, floating, swimming and jumping your way down a turquoise river canyon, ending at the famous Kawasan Falls. Accredited guides lead the route and help you on every jump (all optional), and many bring a camera to capture the action. Expect a few hours in the water, cliff jumps of different heights, natural rock slides and lots of laughter. It's high-adrenaline but beginner-friendly, and you'll leave with a camera roll full of jump shots. Go on a sunny dry-season morning, when the water glows bright blue.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (around December to May); start in the morning

places.name: Badoc Island
places.description: An uninhabited island with white sand, clear water and rocky points to climb, just a short boat ride off Badoc! Hop on a bangka from La Virgen Milagrosa Cove and in about 25 minutes you're stepping onto an island with no resorts and no crowds. Snorkel the clear shallows, free dive off the rocks, scramble over the rock formations for the view, and watch the boatmen point out the sandbar that sinks and reappears with the tide. There are no stores, toilets or showers, so pack food, water and a trash bag, and get back on the boat before dark, since overnight stays are not allowed!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, around November to May, on calm-sea mornings. Follow the boatmen's return time, which depends on the tide.

places.name: Bagasbas Beach
places.description: Bagasbas is the surfing capital of Bicol, and the vibe is pure beach town! The long dark-sand beach faces the open Pacific, so the waves roll in almost all year, and you will see surfers from sunrise to sunset. Take a beginner lesson with a local instructor, watch the pros, or just walk the shore and catch the golden sunrise. Behind it runs the long coastal boulevard, great for a morning jog or an easy bike ride, with casual restaurants and surf shops nearby. Tip: go early for glassy waves and calmer water, and swim only near the lifeguards and flagged areas because the currents here are strong.
places.best_time_to_visit: September to May for the best surf; early morning for sunrise and glassy waves.

places.name: Baguio Night Market
places.description: Thrift hunters, assemble! Every night, Harrison Road beside Burnham Park closes to cars and turns into a long strip of tents selling thrifted jackets, coats, jeans, bags and shoes at bargain prices. Dig through the racks for that perfect vintage find, haggle nicely, then refuel with cheap street food: grilled skewers, fishballs, Korean snacks and hot soup in the cold mountain air. It is crowded and chaotic in the best way, a favorite of students and friend groups. Come early in the night for first pick and thinner crowds.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early in the night; weekdays are less crowded.

places.name: Baguio City Public Market
places.description: Want the real Baguio? Head to the market! The Baguio City Public Market is a sprawling, busy maze where locals shop for highland vegetables, fresh strawberries, cut flowers, longganisa and mountain coffee, plus woven fabrics, beads and wood carvings from around the Cordillera. It is the best place for budget take-home treats like strawberry jam, peanut brittle, ube jam and walis tambo (brooms), usually cheaper than tourist shops. Wander the aisles, haggle politely and grab a quick, cheap meal at the small eateries inside. Go early in the morning when the produce is freshest and the aisles are still breathable.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning (around 6-10 AM), on weekdays.

places.name: Bahay Modernismo
places.description: Step into a 1950s Filipino home, and it is free! Bahay Modernismo is a heritage museum inside Quezon Memorial Circle that rebuilds a mid-century modern bungalow using items from an Aquino family house on Times Street. Walk from the garage and lanai to the living room, kitchen, bedrooms and a mancave, all dressed in bright retro colors, with old radios, TVs, toys and a vintage car. There is also a small gallery of Quezon City infrastructure models. It is a quick, photogenic stop that pairs well with a walk around the Circle and the new elevated promenade. Tip: go on a weekday morning, since it closes at 4 PM and is closed on Mondays.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings, Tuesday to Sunday between 9 AM and 4 PM; closed Mondays.

places.name: Bakhawan Eco-Park
places.description: A whole forest of mangroves planted by hand, right outside Kalibo! Bakhawan Eco-Park started in 1990 on a muddy shoreline and has grown into a 220-hectare mangrove forest run by the community group KASAMA. Walk the 1.3-kilometer boardwalk deep under the canopy until it opens onto the beach, paddle a kayak or ride a bamboo raft through the channels, and plant a mangrove of your own. Brave foodies can ask the keepers for fresh tamilok! It's a perfect stop before or after your Boracay flight.
places.best_time_to_visit: Any dry day; late afternoon is cooler for the long boardwalk.

places.name: Balabac Island Hopping (Onuk Island and Sandbars)
places.description: This is Palawan at its wildest! Balabac sits at the far southern tip of Palawan, where powder-white sandbars and see-through turquoise water look almost unreal. Highlights include Onuk Island, Punta Sebaring, Candaraman Island and the Mansalangan and Starfish sandbars. Getting there is part of the adventure: tours leave Puerto Princesa around 3 AM for the long drive to Buliluyan Port, then boats take you across. Expect glamping tents, generator power only at night and zero mobile signal. Book a 4-day, 3-night accredited tour, bring cash, and go from December to May for calmer seas!
places.best_time_to_visit: December to May; March to May for the clearest sandbar photos.

places.name: Balicasag Island (and Pamilacan Dolphin Watching)
places.description: The highlight of any Panglao island-hopping trip! Boats leave around dawn to look for dolphins near Pamilacan, then head to Balicasag, a marine sanctuary off Alona Beach and Bohol's most famous dive spot. Its corals sit so shallow that you slide off the boat gently, and then the reef plunges into dramatic underwater walls. Snorkelers float over corals, schools of jacks and often sea turtles, while divers explore the drop-offs. Many tours end at Virgin Island's sandbar. Go early in the dry season for calm seas and the best dolphin chances. A worth-it half day for the whole family.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May; leave around 6 AM for dolphins.

places.name: Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park
places.description: Two crater lakes in the middle of the rainforest! Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park hides Lake Balinsasayao and Lake Danao in thick mountain forest above Sibulan, separated by a narrow ridge. Paddle a kayak across the misty, glassy water, walk the forest trails and listen for birds, including the endangered Visayan tarictic hornbill. The air is cool and early mornings feel almost mystical. In 2025 the park was named an ASEAN Heritage Park, so this is Negros Oriental nature at its best. Bring a light jacket and come early.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for mist and calm water.

places.name: Baluarte de San Diego
places.description: A 16th-century fort shaped like an ace of spades! Baluarte de San Diego started in 1586 to 1587 as the round Fort Nuestra Señora de Guia, designed by Jesuit priest Antonio Sedeño, and its circular stone remains still sit inside the later spade-shaped bastion. Buried under soil, the old fort survived the 1945 Battle of Manila, then was excavated in 1979 and restored by 1992. Today it is a peaceful garden with lawns, pergolas and old walls you can walk on, a quieter alternative to Fort Santiago. Go late afternoon for soft light and cooler air, and wear good shoes for the uneven stone.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon on weekdays

places.name: Banaue Rice Terraces Viewpoint
places.description: This is the classic Banaue view! From the main viewpoint, a short ride from town, rice terraces cascade down the valley in giant green steps, carved by Ifugao farmers over generations. The view deck has souvenir shops, and elders in traditional Ifugao attire pose for photos for a small tip. It is the easiest way to see Banaue's terraces without a long trek, and a great stop before heading to Batad. Come in the morning, before the clouds roll in, for the clearest view of the green steps.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning before the clouds roll in

places.name: Bangui Windmills
places.description: The Ilocos photo everyone takes! Twenty giant wind turbines stand in a single row along the shore of Bangui Bay, each about 70 meters tall, turning slowly above the dark sand. Walk the beach right under them, feel the strong sea breeze, and grab snacks and souvenirs from the stalls near the viewing area. It's a quick stop on the way to or from Pagudpud, and an easy add-on to Kapurpurawan and Cape Bojeador. Best moment: late afternoon into sunset, when the light turns golden behind the blades.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to sunset; dry season (November to May)

places.name: Bantay Abot Cave
places.description: A grassy sea hill with a hole punched right through it! Bantay Abot Cave stands on the rocky shore of Balaoi, and the waves of the open sea crash around it while you frame the opening for that classic Pagudpud photo. Walk down to the rocks at low tide, peek through the gap and watch the surf from the little viewpoint. It is an easy stop on a day that also covers Patapat Viaduct and Kabigan Falls!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, November to May; come at low tide in the morning for calmer water and softer light.

places.name: Barasoain Church
places.description: This is where the Philippines first became a republic! Barasoain Church in Malolos, first built by Augustinian missionaries, hosted the Malolos Congress, the country's first legislature, from September 15, 1898. On January 23, 1899, Emilio Aguinaldo took his oath here as president of the First Philippine Republic. Today it is a National Shrine with a museum in the old convent, and older Filipinos know it from the back of the old 10-peso bill. Tour the church and museum, then walk the Kamestisuhan district of ancestral houses and the Casa Real Shrine nearby. Finish with Bulacan sweets like pastillas and ensaymada. Go on a weekday morning, when weddings are fewer.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; weekends are busy with weddings

places.name: Barracuda Lake
places.description: A lake with a hot secret! Barracuda Lake sits behind limestone walls on Coron Island, right beside Kayangan, and it's one of the most unusual dive sites around. Fresh and salt water mix in layers you can feel: once divers pass about 18 meters, the water suddenly turns warm. Even snorkelers love floating over jagged underwater rock formations in glass-clear water. You reach it with a short climb over rocks from the boat dock, and it's part of Coron's ultimate-style island tours. Go in the morning during the dry season, bring snorkel gear and aqua shoes, and enjoy the eerie, beautiful silence.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (November-May), morning

places.name: Basco Lighthouse (Naidi Hills)
places.description: The white Basco Lighthouse sits on Naidi Hills, a short ride from town, and it is the best sunset seat in Batanes! The six-story tower has a spiral staircase up to a fifth-floor viewing deck, with a sweeping view of Basco, Mount Iraya and, on clear days, Sabtang. Come about an hour before sunset, then walk the grassy slopes as the sky turns orange. It is about 1.2 km uphill from Basco Port, so it is an easy first-day stop after landing.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon to sunset, December to May for clear skies

places.name: Basilica Minore del Santo Niño
places.description: The spiritual heart of Cebu! Founded on April 28, 1565, the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño is home to the Santo Niño de Cebu, the image that arrived with Magellan in 1521, was given to the Queen of Cebu, and was found again 44 years later when Legazpi's expedition landed. Devotees pack it daily, and the whole city celebrates during Sinulog every January. Watch candle vendors dance their prayers outside, visit the small museum, and walk over to Magellan's Cross next door. Go on a weekday morning for a calmer visit. An essential stop on any Cebu heritage walk.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; January for Sinulog (very crowded)

places.name: Batad Rice Terraces
places.description: Rice terraces shaped like a giant amphitheater! Batad is a huge bowl of terraces built by Ifugao farmers, part of the UNESCO-listed Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras. No cars reach the village, so you ride to the Saddle and walk down the last stretch, which keeps it quiet and real. Stay overnight in a homestay, wake up to mist over the terraces, then hike to Tappiya Falls for a swim and climb the viewpoints for the classic amphitheater shot. The fields shift from green to gold to mirror-like through the year. Worth every step, promise.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months for easier trails; early morning for mist over the terraces

places.name: BenCab Museum
places.description: Art, pine air and a garden trail in one stop! Founded in 2009 by National Artist Benedicto 'BenCab' Cabrera, this four-level museum on Asin Road is one of the best art spaces in the country. Galleries cover BenCab's own works (including his famous Sabel series), contemporary Filipino art, prints, an Erotica gallery and a strong Cordillera collection of bulul and indigenous pieces. Below the building, the Farm and Garden EcoTrail winds past a duck pond, coffee plants and traditional Ifugao, Kalinga and Bontoc huts. End with lunch or coffee at Cafe Sabel, which looks out over the pond and mountains. Worth it even for non-museum people, and perfect on a foggy Baguio day.
places.best_time_to_visit: Tuesday to Sunday mornings (closed Mondays); weekdays are calmer

opening_hours.note: Last entry 5:30 PM; closed Christmas Day and New Year's Day

places.name: Betis Church (Santiago Apostol Parish)
places.description: Look up! Betis Church is called the Sistine Chapel of the Philippines for its ceiling, painted wall to wall with saints, angels and scenes that look carved but are flat paint tricking your eye. The baroque church in Betis, Guagua, is a National Cultural Treasure, with a gold retablo and a grand baroque facade. Visit between Masses, dress modestly and take your time with the details!
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings, outside Mass times.

places.name: Biak-na-Bato National Park
places.description: A history lesson and a nature trip in one! Biak-na-Bato National Park in San Miguel, Bulacan is a limestone gorge of rivers, forest trails and caves, where General Emilio Aguinaldo set up the revolutionary Republic of Biak-na-Bato. With a local guide, explore Aguinaldo Cave, his old hideout, and Paniki Cave, the bat cave, then cool off in the river pools on calm days. Wildlife lovers might spot the rare Biak-na-Bato limestone frog. It's an easy weekend day trip from Manila. Best moment: a dry-season morning, before the midday heat.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (November to May), weekday mornings

places.name: Bilar Man-Made Forest
places.description: Bohol's famous green tunnel! Between Loboc and Bilar, rows of tall mahogany trees close over the highway into a shady, cinematic tunnel, and the air feels noticeably cooler. The Bilar Man-Made Forest was planted in a reforestation drive in the 1940s and 1950s, and it sits right on the road to the Chocolate Hills, so it's a quick photo stop on the classic countryside tour. Pull over at a safe spot, snap your shots of the canopy, and breathe in the forest air for a few minutes. Fifteen to twenty minutes is enough; just keep off the road and watch for passing vehicles.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon, in daylight

opening_hours.note: Roadside forest along the Loboc-Bilar highway

places.name: Binondo Chinatown
places.description: Time for a food crawl in one of the oldest Chinatowns in the world! Binondo was founded in 1594 for Chinese settlers across the river from Intramuros, and today it's Manila's busiest food-and-trade district. Start at Binondo Church, the Minor Basilica of San Lorenzo Ruiz with its octagonal bell tower, then walk Ongpin Street for dumplings, hopia and lumpia from old family shops. Pick four or five stops instead of queueing everywhere, and slow down between bites to see the old streets and Escolta nearby. Best moment: a weekday morning, before the lunch crowd, with an empty stomach and small bills ready.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; Chinese New Year for festive vibes, but expect huge crowds

places.name: Binurong Point
places.description: Think Batanes, but on Happy Island! Binurong Point is a short hike to a green clifftop where rolling hills drop straight into the deep blue Pacific, with grazing cows and wild coastline all around. Walk the traverse trail to the cliff edge for drone-worthy views, sit on the grass and watch the waves crash far below. Locals hire guides who know the trail and the best photo spots. Tip: go at sunrise or late afternoon for soft light and cooler air, wear shoes with good grip because the trail gets muddy, and stay well back from the cliff edge when it is windy.
places.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise or late afternoon; dry months (March to June) are best, and the trail is muddy after rain.

places.name: Biri Island Rock Formations
places.description: Giant rocks that look like they're from another planet! Biri has seven massive rock formations facing the open Pacific, led by Magasang, Magsapad and Bel-at. Walk out to Bel-at and dip in the clear tidal pools, then hop on a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) to Magasang and Magsapad, where huge waves smash against the cliffs. The whole area is the Biri-Larosa Protected Landscape and Seascape, so stay on the trails and leave no trash. Go early for softer light and calmer heat, or stay for sunset when the rocks glow gold. Bring cash and enough water for a full day out. Worth the trip for the photos alone!
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for calm seas and dry weather; go at low tide to reach the tidal pools

places.name: Bitbit River and Ipo Dam View Deck
places.description: A clear mountain river less than 2 hours from Manila! Ride up Ipo Road into the Sierra Madre, stop at the Ipo Dam View Deck for the valley view, then head down to Bitbit River, where families and riders wade in the cool water under the tall Bitbit Bridge. Rent a hut by the river, bring lunch and spend the afternoon in the shallows. It is the Bulacan summer escape that even made national TV on GMA's Kapuso Mo, Jessica Soho!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, March to May, on weekday mornings; stay away during heavy rain and dam water releases.

places.name: Black Island (Malajon Island)
places.description: Black limestone cliffs, white sand and a cave with a pool inside! Black Island, called Malajon by locals, sits off the northwestern coast of Busuanga in northern Palawan. Step into the main cave to find a soaring, cathedral-like chamber with stalactites and a clear freshwater pool. Outside, snorkel the coral gardens and look for the small shipwreck just off the beach. It is far from Coron town, so most people visit on a Calauit Safari tour with a Black Island side trip, or ride to Salvacion and hire a bangka for the short crossing. Pack snacks and water shoes!
places.best_time_to_visit: Leave early: it is about 3 hours from Coron town (2 hours by van, 1 hour by boat).

places.name: Blackbird at the Nielson Tower
places.description: Dinner inside an old airport tower? Only at Blackbird! The restaurant fills the Art Deco Nielson Tower, built in 1937 as the terminal and control tower of Manila's first commercial airport, right inside Ayala Triangle. A spiral staircase leads up to The Cabin, the old control tower, now a private dining room, and the garden terrace sits where the tarmac used to be. The menu mixes world classics with contemporary Asian cooking, and the MICHELIN Guide lists it in its Manila selection. It's a go-to for anniversaries, farewell dinners and business lunches. Best moment: dinner on the terrace as the Ayala Triangle lights come on, or a slow weekend brunch or afternoon tea.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dinner for the terrace and lights; weekend brunch

places.name: Blue Lagoon (Maira-ira Beach)
places.description: White sand, blue water, green hills: Blue Lagoon is Pagudpud at its most postcard-perfect! This bay at Maira-ira Point, in one of Luzon's northernmost towns, faces the Dos Hermanos islets, with thick forest running down to fine white sand and crystal-blue water. On calm days it's ideal for swimming, and it's a favorite of windsurfers when the wind picks up. It's more developed than Saud Beach but still far quieter than the big southern beaches. Make it a half day, then add Kabigan Falls or the Patapat Viaduct on the drive.
places.best_time_to_visit: March-May for calm, clear water; weekdays for fewer people

places.name: Bohol Bee Farm
places.description: A farm-to-table lunch on a cliff over the Bohol Sea! Bohol Bee Farm in Dao, Dauis is an organic farm resort known for its edible flower salad, homemade breads with spreads like pesto and honey, and homemade ice cream in local flavors. Take the farm tour to see the beekeeping and organic gardens, then eat with the sea view. Before you leave, raid the Buzzz Shop for honey products and spreads to take home. Go for lunch or an afternoon snack, about 15 minutes from Alona Beach. A healthy, relaxed stop on any Panglao trip with the family.
places.best_time_to_visit: Lunch or afternoon snack

places.name: Bolinao Falls 1, 2 and 3
places.description: Three falls, one day, one easy road trip! Bolinao Falls is a cluster of three waterfalls a few minutes apart in Samang Norte, inland from the beaches. Falls 1 is the star: about 20 feet tall, deep green-blue water, and a high wooden platform you can jump from. Falls 2 is a 3-minute drive away. It's smaller, but the pool is wide with shallow parts for kids, and you park right by the river. Falls 3 has a turquoise basin that looks like a resort pool, plus shallow pools on top and picnic huts. Life vests are required everywhere (₱50 rental, or bring your own), and Falls 1 and 3 have steep stairs. Go on a weekday morning, and pair it with Patar Beach for sunset.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for the fewest people. The dry season (around November to May) gives the clearest water. During heavy rain or typhoon advisories, the LGU or DOT can close sites temporarily (as in July 2025).

places.name: Bomod-ok Falls
places.description: Sagada's 'Big Falls', and worth every step! Bomod-ok is a tall, powerful waterfall reached by a scenic trek down through the stone-walled rice terraces and small villages of Bangaan and Fidelisan. The walk is half the magic: farmers tending their fields, terraces all around, and the roar of water getting louder as you go. At the bottom, a cold, misty pool waits for a quick dip if the current allows. The climb back up is the sweaty part, so pace yourself and bring water. A local guide is required, and it's one of the best half-day trips in Sagada.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry-season mornings, November to May

places.name: Bonbon Beach and Sandbar
places.description: One of the World's 50 Best Beaches, two years in a row! Bonbon Beach on Romblon Island has a long, powdery sandbar that curves out toward little Bang-og Island, and at low tide you can walk all the way across through shallow, clear water. The beach faces west, so the late afternoon light here is gorgeous. It is rustic and simple, with no big resorts, just sand, sea and the green hills of Romblon town behind you. It is a short tricycle ride from the port, so come early on weekends before the crowd arrives!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, November to May. Arrive before 9 AM on weekends, and time your walk across the sandbar with low tide.

places.name: Boracay Sunset Paraw Sailing
places.description: The most Boracay thing to do at golden hour! Hop on a paraw, a traditional Filipino outrigger sailboat, and sit on the netting while it glides along White Beach as the sky turns orange and pink. With nothing but wind in the sail, it's quiet, breezy and very photogenic. Rides usually last 30 minutes to an hour, and the boatmen are pros at taking your photos. Sunset slots are the most popular, so book ahead or arrive early to pick a boat on the beach. Best moment: the last half hour before sunset, with your partner or friends and the water splashing up through the net.
places.best_time_to_visit: Around 5 PM to sunset, November to May

places.name: Borawan Island
places.description: Borawan got its name from Boracay plus Palawan, and one look explains why! Bright sand meets tall limestone rocks and clear Tayabas Bay water, all just a short boat ride from Padre Burgos. Swim in the calm cove, climb around the rock formations for photos, and kayak along the cliffs. Pitch a tent for the night or rent a cottage, then wake up to a quiet sunrise over the bay. Make it a full island-hopping day by adding Dampalitan Island, with its long beach lined with pine trees, plus Puting Buhangin and the swim-through cave of Kwebang Lampas. Bring cash and food from town, since stores on the island are few.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May (dry season); weekdays to skip the summer crowds; low tide makes the rocks easier to explore.

places.name: Britania Group of Islands
places.description: Mindanao's island-hopping star! Britania is a group of 24 islands and islets scattered across Lianga Bay off San Agustin, Surigao del Sur, facing the Pacific. Hop to Boslon, the biggest island, then Naked Island, a bare white sandbar, and leafy Hiyor-hiyoran, with plenty of stops for swimming and snorkeling. It's far less crowded than the big-name beaches, so expect quiet shores and local-run boats. Pair it with Enchanted River in Hinatuan and Tinuy-an Falls in Bislig for a Surigao del Sur loop. Bring food, water and cash, use reef-safe sunscreen, and head out in the morning while the sea is calm.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to September when the sea is calmer

places.name: Bugtong Bato Falls and Kawa Hot Bath
places.description: Antique's best adventure combo! A 25-minute forest trail from the Tuno barangay hall leads to the first tier of seven-tier Bugtong Bato Falls, a tall white ribbon of water over a cool pool. Afterwards, soak in a kawa, a giant old sugar cauldron filled with warm water and flowers, right on the banks of the Tibiao River. It works as a long day trip from Caticlan and Boracay!
places.best_time_to_visit: After the rains start (June to November) for fuller falls; start early.

places.name: Buhawi Hills
places.description: Rolling green ridges above a braided river valley! Buhawi Hills in Pio Duran is a grassy eco-trek with knife-edge ridgelines, a river snaking far below and mountains stacked to the horizon. The climb takes a few hours with a registered local guide, and the 360-degree view at the top is the payoff. Start at sunrise for the best light and cooler air!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season; sunrise starts.

places.name: Bulabog Beach (Kitesurfing)
places.description: Kites, sails and non-stop wind: Bulabog is Boracay's other beach, and during Amihan season it becomes one of Asia's top spots for kitesurfing and windsurfing! The northeast wind blows straight onshore, filling the bay with colorful kites. Watch the action from the sand with a drink, or sign up for a beginner lesson at one of the kite and windsurf schools along the shore. It's a short walk across the island from White Beach, and it feels sportier and more local than the main strip. Come on a windy afternoon from around November to March for the best show.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to March for steady Amihan winds

places.name: Bulusan Lake (Bulusan Volcano Natural Park)
places.description: A calm, deep-green crater lake wrapped in rainforest, with the volcano peeking through the clouds! Bulusan Lake is the star of Bulusan Volcano Natural Park, and it is one of the prettiest chill spots in Bicol. Ride the e-jeep in from the eco-center, paddle a kayak or SUP, take a boat with a local paddler, or walk the shore trail under big trees. Bring snacks, because there is a view deck and picnic spots. Tip: go early in the morning, when the water is glassy and the mountain is clear. Bulusan Volcano is active, so stay on the lake trails and follow park staff.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months, March to June; go early morning for still water and clear views. Check PHIVOLCS status first.

places.name: Buntod Sandbar and Reef Marine Sanctuary
places.description: Just 15 minutes by boat from Masbate City, a strip of powdery white sand rises out of blue-green water! Buntod Sandbar sits inside the Buntod Reef Marine Sanctuary, a protected area full of corals and fish. Walk the sandbar at low tide, snorkel over the reef, rent a kayak or a water bike, or join a guided reef tour. Stilt cottages give you shade between swims. Register and pay the small environmental fee at the tourism desk before you board, and go on a weekday morning for the calmest, emptiest sandbar!
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings at low tide, when the sandbar is fully out. Open about 7 AM to 5 PM.

places.name: Burias Island Hopping (Animasola, Tinalisayan, Sombrero)
places.description: Rock formations, a sandbar and a beach camp, all in one day! The classic Burias circuit from San Pascual, Masbate visits Animasola Island with its dramatic rock formations, Tinalisayan Island and its tidal sandbar, and Sombrero Island, where you can camp right on the beach. Every stop feels different, and the whole area still feels raw and uncrowded. Charter a boat with your group, bring enough cash in small bills (there are no ATMs on Burias), and leave early to beat the afternoon chop on the Ragay Gulf!
places.best_time_to_visit: March to late May for the calmest seas; November to December is quieter but carries some typhoon risk.

places.name: Burnham Park
places.description: Baguio's green heart just got a glow-up! Burnham Park, the 33-hectare park named after American architect Daniel Burnham, who drew up the city's plan in 1903, is the easiest pine-shaded break downtown. Its lake reopened on September 1, 2026, after nearly 11 months of rehabilitation, with a new boardwalk and boating back in action, so rent a boat and paddle around. Then pedal a rental bike, visit the Rose Garden, or just people-watch under the pines with strawberry taho. It's free, open all day, and a short walk from Session Road. Go early on a weekday morning for cool air, calm water and good photo light.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early weekday mornings (6-9 AM); expect crowds on Panagbenga weekends

places.name: Buruwisan Falls (Mount Romelo)
places.description: Hike through the Sierra Madre foothills and get rewarded with a waterfall party! Buruwisan Falls is the star of Mount Romelo, dropping about 50 meters into a big natural pool hidden in a forest gorge. The trail is a beginner climb over a low hill, so you can focus on the fun: river crossings, forest shade and a swim under the falls. Camp on the plateau above and hop to the other cascades nearby, like Lanzones, Sampaloc and Batya-Batya Falls. Register at Barangay Macatad and hire a local guide. Go in the dry months, wear shoes with strong grip, and pack a dry bag, because the clay trail turns into slippery mud after rain.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May (dry season); start early in the morning; avoid days after heavy rain.

places.name: Buwakan ni Alejandra
places.description: A hillside flower garden in the mountains of Cebu! Buwakan ni Alejandra (buwak means flower) is packed with more than 200 species of local blooms, perched on the side of a mountain in Gaas, Balamban. The farm blooms in phases, so the colors change through the year, and every corner is made for photos. It's open daily from 6 AM, so come early for soft light, wear comfy shoes for the slopes and check the farm's page for what's in bloom before you go!
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for soft light (open daily 6 AM to 6 PM); check the farm page for the current bloom phase.

places.name: Cabongaoan Beach and Death Pool
places.description: Creamy white sand, limestone rocks and a famous natural pool! Cabongaoan Beach is a long, quiet cove on Pangasinan's western coast, and a short walk away sits the Death Pool, a deep rock pool that fills with clear sea water when the tide drops. Spend the day on the sand, walk out to the pool at low tide and stay for one of the best sunsets in the province. Come outside summer and you might have it almost to yourselves!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, March to May; plan your Death Pool visit for low tide, usually in the afternoon.

places.name: Cagayan de Oro White Water Rafting
places.description: Paddle hard, scream louder! White water rafting on the Cagayan de Oro River is the city's signature adventure and the ultimate group adrenaline day in Northern Mindanao. Outfitters take you from the jump-off in Barangay Mambuaya, about 45 minutes from the city, down a run of rapids past limestone cliffs and green hills. Beginner runs are full of splashes and laughs, while advanced routes go further and rougher. Guides handle the steering and safety, and packages usually include gear and transfers. Wear clothes you don't mind getting soaked, and go in the morning so you're back in the city for lunch.
places.best_time_to_visit: Mornings; year-round for beginner runs

places.name: Cagbalete Island
places.description: Cagbalete is the big, wild beach island of Quezon, and its low-tide sandbar is the star! When the water pulls back, a huge stretch of pale sand opens up, and you can walk far out into Lamon Bay. Take the boat from Mauban Port, settle into a rustic beachfront resort or pitch a tent, then spend the day swimming, kayaking and snorkeling. Cruise the mangrove river, hunt for rock formations at Sitio Buntis, and stay up for a sky full of stars. Stay overnight because the trip from Manila is long and the boat times are fixed. Book your resort before you go, since the port follows a strict no booking, no sailing rule.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for calm seas and the best sandbar days; go overnight and plan around the low tide.

places.name: Cagnipa Rolling Hills
places.description: Batanes vibes with a Bicol address! Cagnipa Rolling Hills in northern Catanduanes is a sweep of grassland rolling down to quiet coves and the open sea, with cows and carabaos grazing along the way. Nearby, a concrete staircase drops to Tuwad-Tuwadan, a natural rock pool shaped by the waves. There are no structures and no crowds, just wind, grass and a huge view. Come in the late afternoon for golden light on the hills.
places.best_time_to_visit: Calm, dry months; avoid typhoon season since Catanduanes faces the Pacific. Late afternoon gives golden light on the hills.

places.name: Cagsawa Ruins and Mayon ATV Tours
places.description: Bicol's most famous view! The lone belfry of Cagsawa Church stands in a park with the near-perfect cone of Mayon Volcano rising behind it. The Franciscan church was rebuilt in 1724, then wrecked along with the town of Cagsawa in Mayon's eruption on February 1, 1814. In 2026 the National Museum declared the ruins a National Cultural Treasure. Snap the classic shot, browse the souvenir stalls, then join an ATV ride across lahar trails and river beds toward Mayon's foot. Best moment: early morning, before clouds cover the summit.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning (6-8 AM); drier months around March to May

places.name: Calauit Safari Park
places.description: A real safari in Palawan! Calauit Safari Park, on a 3,700-hectare island in northern Busuanga, is where giraffes and zebras roam free, descendants of African animals shipped here in 1977. Rangers take you around the island, and on many tours you get to feed the giraffes. The park also protects Philippine species like the Calamian deer, Palawan mouse-deer and civet cats. It's a long day from Coron town, so most tours add a beach stop after. Super fun with kids and a unique break from lagoons and lakes. Best moment: morning feeding time in the dry season.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (November to May); morning for feeding

places.name: Caleruega Church (Transfiguration Chapel)
places.description: A rustic chapel on a hilltop, wrapped in gardens and mountain views! Caleruega, home of the Chapel of the Transfiguration, was founded by the Dominican Order in 1994 and named after Caleruega in Spain, the birthplace of Saint Dominic. Climb the Dominican Steps through the landscaped gardens to the chapel, then look out over green ridges toward Mount Batulao. It is one of the most loved wedding venues near Tagaytay, so you might spot a bride! Entry is only ₱30, and the grounds are open daily from 6 AM to 5:30 PM.
places.best_time_to_visit: Open daily, 6 AM to 5:30 PM.

places.name: Calicoan Island
places.description: The Visayas surf escape without the Siargao crowds! Calicoan sits at the southern tip of Samar, facing the open Pacific. On the east side, ABCD Beach gets some of the most consistent waves in the country, and surfers of every level paddle out almost every day of the year. On the west side, Banago's white-sand beaches stay calm in the Amihan months, great for a swim and a sunset. Squeeze in a dip in the blue cave lagoon of Linao and you have the whole island in one trip. Fly to Tacloban, ride about four hours to Guiuan, and stay a few days!
places.best_time_to_visit: Waves come most of the year, with the biggest swells from passing low-pressure systems; the Banago side is calmest in the Amihan months, roughly November to March.

places.name: Callao Cave
places.description: Callao Cave is Cagayan's best-known natural attraction and a real history spot! Climb about 187 steps to the entrance, then walk through seven limestone chambers. One of the big chambers is a natural chapel, with an altar lit by sunlight streaming through holes in the roof. Fossils found here starting in 2007 were later named Homo luzonensis, a human species that lived about 50,000 to 67,000 years ago. Hard hats are now required inside. After the cave, take a boat on the Pinacanauan River for a swim or a riverside picnic. Pair it with a bowl of pancit batil patong in Tuguegarao.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning, when sunlight enters the chapel chamber; dry season (December-May)

places.name: Calle Crisologo
places.description: Like stepping back in time! Calle Crisologo is the cobblestone heart of Vigan, which UNESCO calls the best-preserved planned Spanish colonial town in Asia. Both sides of the street are lined with old bahay na bato (stone houses) with capiz windows, heavy wooden floors and balconies, many now antique shops, cafes and souvenir stores. Walk it early in the morning for empty-street photos, then come back at night when the warm lamps light up the facades. Hop on a kalesa, shop for abel Iloko blankets, and snack on empanada at nearby Plaza Burgos. One of the most photogenic streets in the country.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for empty-street photos; evening for the lamplit look; November-May dry season

opening_hours.note: Public heritage street; shops keep their own hours

places.name: Cambugahay Falls
places.description: Siquijor's star attraction: tiered turquoise pools flowing through the jungle in Lazi! Swing from the famous rope swing, ride a bamboo raft, or just soak in the cool water with your friends. You'll walk down 135 concrete steps from the road, and a small entrance fee is collected at the top. Arrive early in the morning, before tour vans and scooters pile in, for clear water and photos without the crowd. Make it a Lazi day: the old Lazi Church, on UNESCO's tentative list, and the centuries-old Enchanted Balete Tree are both nearby.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning; dry season for the clearest water

places.name: Camotes Islands (Santiago Bay and Lake Danao)
places.description: Camotes is Cebu's laid-back island escape: three islands, slow roads, white-sand coves and cave pools, about two hours by ferry from Danao. Base yourself in San Francisco on Pacijan Island, home of Santiago Bay, the long white public beach, and Lake Danao, an inland lake for kayaking and boat rides. Rent a motorbike and loop the island: swim in the freshwater pool inside Timubo Cave, jump at Buho Rock, chill at the turquoise Mangodlong Rock cove, then cross the 1.5-km causeway to Poro for Bukilat Cave. Stay at least one night, catch sunset on the west coast, and book the early ferry back on weekends.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months (roughly February to May) for calm seas; weekdays for empty beaches.

places.name: Camp John Hay
places.description: Pine trees, cool air and a lot of history: Camp John Hay is Baguio's leafiest hangout! It began in the early 1900s as an American base, and today it's a forest and tourist area run by the BCDA. Walk the shaded Yellow Trail under the pines, then head to the Historical Core for the Bell House, Bell Amphitheater and the quirky Cemetery of Negativism, where you can 'bury' your bad vibes. Families and friends can try the ziplines and canopy rides at Tree Top Adventure. It's calmer and cooler than downtown, so it's made for a slow morning walk, a date or a picnic on the lawns.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for the trails; November-April for dry, cool weather

places.name: Campuestohan Highland Resort
places.description: Larger than life, literally! Campuestohan Highland Resort in the cool hills of Talisay City, Negros Occidental is the kitschy theme-park resort famous for its giant King Kong, dinosaurs and its Guinness-record chicken-shaped hotel. Spend the day riding the zipline across the resort, splashing in the pools and wave pools, wandering the dino park and posing at every giant statue. The highland air is cooler than Bacolod and the views stretch down to the plains. It's loud, colorful and super family-friendly; new record-chasing attractions keep popping up. Best moment: a clear weekday morning, or December nights when the Christmas village lights up.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for clear views; December for the Christmas village

places.name: CamSur Watersports Complex (CWC)
places.description: Wakeboarding in Bicol, let's go! The CamSur Watersports Complex (CWC) in Pili, about 20 minutes from Naga City, has been called the mecca of water sports parks in the Philippines since it opened in 2006. Beginners start with kneeboarding on the beginner cable while pros hit the ramps and sliders on the main lake, and there's also water-skiing, an inflatable aquapark and boat rides. Board, vest and helmet rentals are on site, plus lockers and cabanas for groups. Even just watching the riders from the lakeside is fun. Go on a sunny dry-season morning or late afternoon, when the water is calm and the heat is softer.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season mornings or late afternoons; weekdays for shorter waits

places.name: Canigao Island
places.description: A ring of white sand, a long wooden boardwalk over clear water and a protected reef: Canigao Island is Leyte's little island escape! It's a 15 to 20-minute public boat ride from the port beside Matalom Plaza, and part of the water around it is a fish sanctuary. Rent a cottage for the day, snorkel the clear shallows, or pitch a tent and stay for both sunset and sunrise.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for the best weather and calmer seas.

places.name: Cape Bojeador Lighthouse
places.description: Over 130 years and still shining! Cape Bojeador Lighthouse was first lit on March 30, 1892, and still guides ships from Vigia de Nagparitan Hill in Burgos, on Luzon's northwest corner. Climb the brick steps up the hill, admire the octagonal brick tower with its brass cupola and the old keeper's buildings, then look out over the West Philippine Sea where Spanish galleons once sailed. It's a top stop on the Ilocos Norte loop and an easy pair with Kapurpurawan nearby. Best moment: late afternoon, when the bricks glow and the sea breeze cools things down.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon; dry season (November to May)

places.name: Capones Island Lighthouse
places.description: A Spanish-era lighthouse on a wild, rocky island: the best view on any Zambales island-hopping trip! Capones Island sits off Pundaquit, all steep cliffs and rock formations ringed by sand and clear water. Boats drop you on the beach, then a short, steep trail climbs to the Faro de Punta Capones, a lighthouse first lit in 1890 that still shines today. From the top, you get sweeping views of the West Philippine Sea and the island's dramatic cliffs. The old keeper's quarters are in ruins, which only adds to the drama. Go in the morning on a calm-sea day, and pair it with Anawangin or Nagsasa Cove.
places.best_time_to_visit: Calm-sea mornings, November to May

places.name: Carabao Island
places.description: Boracay's quiet neighbour is just one boat ride away! Carabao Island, called Hambil by locals, sits just north of Boracay in Romblon and is a town of its own, San Jose. Expect fine white-sand beaches, clear blue water and cliff-jumping spots, minus the crowds. Ride the public boat from Caticlan for a day trip, or stay two nights and slow down for sunsets you almost have to yourself.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months; plan boat days around good weather since inter-island trips depend on the schedule.

places.name: Caramoan Island Hopping (Matukad, Lahos, Sabitang Laya)
places.description: Survivor-level beauty! Caramoan in Camarines Sur is all dramatic limestone islets, powdery white-sand coves and clear water, so wild that many international editions of Survivor were filmed here. A day of island hopping from Paniman usually covers Matukad with its hidden lagoon, Lahos and Sabitang Laya, plus snorkeling stops and Gota beach. Getting here takes effort, which keeps it uncrowded and raw. Eat kinalas in town, sleep in a simple beachfront homestay, and plan for a full travel day each way. Best moment: calm summer seas, March to June.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to June for calmer seas

places.name: Carnaza Island
places.description: Cebu's far-north island for people who like it quiet! Carnaza, off Daanbantayan, has turquoise coves, white beaches and rugged cliffs. Swim and cliff-jump at Liog-Liog Cove, peek into the legend-filled Skull Cove, beach-hop to Candionesio and Linao, then camp under a sky full of stars. Getting there takes a long bus ride and a boat, and that's exactly why it stays this unspoiled.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, when the boat crossing is calmer.

places.name: Casa Manila
places.description: Ever wondered how a rich family lived in 1800s Manila? Casa Manila in Plaza San Luis, Intramuros, shows you room by room! Its facade is patterned after an 1850s house that once stood on Jaboneros Street in Binondo, and inside you'll find period furniture, a grand sala, capiz windows and an old-style kitchen. Think of it as a lifestyle museum rather than an original ancestral house, and that's what makes it fun to explore. Go on a weekday morning, take it slow, and pair it with San Agustin Church nearby.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; closed Mondays

places.name: Casapsapan Beach
places.description: A 2.5 km curve of fine, pale sand backed by jungle, with turquoise Pacific water rolling in: Casapsapan is the reward at the end of a long road! This is Casiguran's most famous beach, far up the Aurora coast, and it rarely feels crowded. Swim and snorkel in the bay when it's calm, camp under the trees, walk to the Casapsapan River mouth at the southeast end and explore the mangroves. Sunrise here is unreal. It's more than 10 hours from Manila, so make it a long weekend!
places.best_time_to_visit: October to May for calmer seas. Sunrise for the best light.

places.name: Casaroro Falls
places.description: Casaroro Falls in Valencia, Negros Oriental drops about 100 feet down a narrow rock canyon into a cold swimming hole, wrapped in thick greenery. Getting there is half the adventure: a long way down, then boulder-hopping along the river, which keeps the crowds small. Your reward is a cool dip and that classic tall-falls photo! It's an easy half-day nature trip from Dumaguete. Go in the morning, wear shoes with grip and save energy for the climb back up.
places.best_time_to_visit: Mornings in the dry season

places.name: Cavinti Underground River and Cave Complex
places.description: Helmet on, headlamp on: real caving near Manila! The Cavinti Underground River and Cave Complex has huge chambers of stalactites and flowstone, a chest-deep underground river and even a small waterfall inside the cave. You register at Bumbungan Eco-Park, ride to the jump-off, cross a bamboo bridge and trek through the forest to the cave mouth, where a local guide leads you in. The basic route is beginner-friendly, so it is a great first spelunking adventure!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months; start early in the morning.

places.name: Cebu Safari and Adventure Park
places.description: Tigers, monkeys, exotic birds and rare reptiles, all in the green hills of northern Cebu! Cebu Safari and Adventure Park in Carmen is a big wildlife park with roomy habitats, plus flower gardens like Michel's Garden, with its huge orchid collection, and the leafy tunnel of the Gardens of the World. Want a thrill? Try the 110-foot Giant Swing, the zipline, the Sky Bike or an ATV ride. Plan a full day, come early, and if you want to wake up in the hills, the park has cabins and glamping tents too.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekdays for the lower rate; come in the morning so you have the whole day.

places.name: Cebu Taoist Temple
places.description: A red-and-gold temple on a hill with one of the best views of Cebu City! The Cebu Taoist Temple in Beverly Hills, Lahug was built by Cebu's Chinese-Filipino community. Enter through a mini Great Wall of China, then climb past dragon-topped roofs to the viewing areas over the city. Worshippers and non-worshippers alike are welcome, as long as you're respectful. Go in the morning or late afternoon for cooler air and softer light. A peaceful stop on Cebu's uphill tour.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon

places.name: Celera
places.description: Dark, moody and full of umami: Celera is a one-Michelin-star dining room on the 3rd floor of Comuna, run by chef-owners Nicco Santos and Quenee Vilar. They call their food 'marriage cuisine': contemporary Asian cooking that blends Japanese, Chinese, Singaporean and other influences, built on dashi, fermentation and a touch of smoke. The black-toned space with an open kitchen sets the mood, plating is artful and service is warm, so it feels lively, not stiff. A true date-night spot, especially if you love bold, savory flavors. Book ahead directly with the restaurant, and come hungry!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dinner, booked in advance

places.name: Chawa View Deck
places.description: Waves smashing into a wall of rock right below you! Chawa View Deck sits on a cliff along Mahatao's coastal road, the classic first stop of a South Batan tour. Lean on the railing for the view of the rugged limestone shore, then, if your legs are up for it, take the steep stairway of about 100 steps down to the sea, where a small pool forms at low tide. Go on a calm, sunny day!
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May on a calm day; low tide for the little pool at the bottom.

places.name: Chocolate Hills Complex
places.description: Bohol's most famous view, and you have to see it in person! Hundreds of cone-shaped limestone hills roll across the Bohol countryside. In the dry season the grass turns cocoa-brown, which gave them their name; in the rainy months they're lush green. Climb the stairs to the viewing deck at the Chocolate Hills Complex in Carmen for the classic panorama, then listen to the local legends of feuding giants. It's the centerpiece of any Bohol countryside tour, alongside the tarsiers and the Loboc River. Go early morning or late afternoon in the dry months, when the hills are brown and the light is soft.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning or late afternoon; around February to May for the brown 'chocolate' look

places.name: Cloud 9 360° View and Hanging Bridge
places.description: Cross a swaying hanging bridge to a 360-degree view deck high above Metro Manila! Cloud 9 on Sumulong Highway in Antipolo is a classic date spot, especially at golden hour, when you can watch the sunset and then see the city lights switch on below. One ticket also gets you into the art gallery and museum on site, and if you eat at the Cloud 9 restaurant, entry can be free with a minimum spend. Come before 4 PM on weekdays to skip the lines, then stay for dinner with a view!
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon into evening for the sunset and city lights; weekdays before 4 PM to avoid lines.

places.name: Cloud 9 Boardwalk
places.description: The wave that made Siargao famous, and in 2026 it joins the world's top surf tour! Cloud 9 is a hollow right-hand reef break off General Luna, the reason the town is called the Surfing Capital of the Philippines. A wooden boardwalk runs over the reef to a viewing platform where you can watch surfers drop into the barrel at sunrise or sunset. The old tower was wrecked by Typhoon Odette in 2021, and a new watchtower started construction in April 2026. Non-surfers can walk the boardwalk, and beginners learn at gentler breaks nearby with an instructor. Go in surf season, roughly August to November, for the best waves and contest buzz.
places.best_time_to_visit: August to November for surf season; sunrise or sunset for the boardwalk

places.name: Communal Ranch
places.description: Welcome to Bukidnon's big-sky country! Communal Ranch in Impasug-ong is a wide green pasture ringed by folded mountains, with horses grazing near a little pond and lone trees straight out of a postcard. Spread out a picnic, take a horse ride across the field, and let the cool mountain breeze do the rest. On some days the Higaonon perform their ritual dances for visitors. It's about two hours from Cagayan de Oro, so come early and stay for the golden light.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon for soft light on the ridges; dry months for clear views.

places.name: Coron WWII Shipwrecks (Skeleton Wreck and Wreck Dives)
places.description: Dive into history! On September 24, 1944, a US Navy air strike sank a Japanese supply fleet sheltering in Coron Bay, and those ships still rest on the seabed today. Non-divers can snorkel over Skeleton Wreck, whose top sits just 5 meters down, on a Tour B or Super Ultimate island-hopping day. Certified divers can go deeper: even newly certified Open Water divers can explore real WWII wrecks here, which makes Coron a bucket-list trip for divers. Book a three-dive day with an accredited dive shop, and go from December to March for the best conditions!
places.best_time_to_visit: December to March for the best diving conditions.

places.name: Corregidor Island
places.description: Step onto The Rock, the island fortress that guarded Manila Bay in World War II! A guided tour brings its war history to life. Ride the tranvia past war ruins and giant gun batteries like Battery Way and Battery Hearn, then walk into Malinta Tunnel, the bomb-proof shelter that became headquarters for General MacArthur and the Philippine President. Finish at the Pacific War Memorial and the lighthouse for sweeping bay views. Today the trip starts in Mariveles, Bataan, with a quick 20-minute boat ride across. Tours are pre-booked day trips, so reserve ahead and leave Manila early. Pack water, snacks and sunscreen, because there is no food for sale on the island!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, November to May, for calmer seas and clear skies. Take the morning tour to beat the midday heat.

places.name: Cresta de Gallo Island
places.description: Picture a long ribbon of powder-white sand curling through water so clear it glows! Cresta de Gallo is a tiny, uninhabited islet off Sibuyan Island in Romblon, and its curving sandbar is the star of the show. There are no resorts and no stalls, just sand, sea and sky, so you get the castaway feeling for real. Base yourself in San Fernando, book a local guide and boat, find other travelers to split the cost, and pack everything you need for the day.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, roughly March to May, for calm seas. Leave early in the morning.

places.name: Crosswinds Tagaytay
places.description: Swiss Alps vibes, about two hours from Manila! Crosswinds is a 100-hectare alpine-style village by Brittany Corporation, wrapped in more than 35,000 pine trees, so the air feels cooler and smells like a real forest. Stroll the pine-lined lanes, snap photos of the colorful Swiss-style chalets, then warm up with coffee and pastries at the cafes inside. Come late afternoon when the fog rolls in, and in the holiday season the Trail of Lights turns the forest into a glowing walk. Entry is per car and most of it comes back as a food voucher, so plan to eat here and make a slow, cozy date out of it!
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings or late afternoons for fog and fewer cars; November to January for the cold season and the Trail of Lights. Cafes are generally open 8 AM–10 PM.

places.name: Crystal Cove Island
places.description: Two sea caves, hidden coves and clear blue water, all on one little island off Boracay! Crystal Cove Island is the favorite add-on to a Boracay island-hopping trip: follow the garden paths, climb down into Cave 1 and Cave 2 where the sea glows turquoise, and take in the ocean views from the lookouts. Bring water shoes and your camera!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, November to May, in the morning before the island-hopping crowds.

places.name: Cuatro Islas
places.description: Four islands in one island-hopping day! Cuatro Islas is a protected landscape and seascape off western Leyte made up of Apid, Digyo, Mahaba and Himokilan. Digyo is the crowd favorite, with white sand, turquoise water and coral reefs for snorkeling. Hop across by pumpboat from Inopacan, pack lunch and water, and stay for a slow afternoon in the shade. The islands were the Visayas' only finalist in the 2025 Para El MAR Awards for well-managed marine protected areas, so don't step on corals and bring your trash back to the mainland.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to June for calm seas

places.name: Cubao Expo
places.description: Vintage finds by day, beer and gigs by night: Cubao Expo is QC's creative hideout! It began as the Marikina Shoe Expo, a hub for locally made shoes, then this compact compound in Araneta City filled up with antique and vintage shops, record stores, galleries, cafes, bars and restaurants. Today it's a favorite hangout for artists, musicians, collectors and anyone tired of mall plans. Come late afternoon to browse, then stay for dinner, drinks and music.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon into the evening; weekends for the liveliest crowd
