places.name: Dagisdis ng Maragondon
places.description: A hilltop nature park made for group days! Dagisdis ng Maragondon has an infinity-style pool facing the Maragondon mountains, giant swings over the valley, net hammocks, a rope bridge and a giant chair for silly photos. Bring your own food, rent a cottage or gazebo, and chill in the breeze all day for a small entrance fee. It is easiest by car, about 2 hours from Manila. Book ahead on weekends!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months; weekdays for fewer people.

places.name: Dahican Beach
places.description: Dahican is Mindanao's surf-and-skim beach: about 7 km of fine pale sand and coconut trees facing the open Pacific in Mati, Davao Oriental. The waves roll in year-round, so take a surf or skimboard lesson, or just watch the local skimboarders show off. Base yourself at a beach resort like Dahican Surf Resort, then fill the day: catch a sea turtle hatchling release in nesting season, fly over the coast in an ultralight plane, or island-hop Pujada Bay. Wake up early for sunrise over the Pacific; the beach faces east!
places.best_time_to_visit: Year-round for surf and skimboarding; March to May for calmer island hopping in Pujada Bay. Come at sunrise.

places.name: Dahilayan Adventure Park
places.description: Fly down a mountain at up to 90 kph! Dahilayan is Bukidnon's highland thrill park, and it doesn't hold back. The headline is the dual zipline: two parallel 840-meter lines launched from about 4,700 feet above sea level, so you can race a friend side by side. Then try the Razorback, billed as the Philippines' first alpine mountain coaster, the Dropzone over a man-made lake, and the Python Rollerzip. The highland air is cool, so bring a jacket. Go on a clear weekday morning for shorter lines.
places.best_time_to_visit: Clear weekday mornings (open daily)

places.name: Daldagon Peak
places.description: A grassy cliff-top path above the open sea! Daldagon Peak in far-flung Siruma gives you sweeping views of rolling hills, forest and the deep blue Pacific, with a white-railed trail running along the ridge. It is a long, rough ride from Naga, which keeps it wonderfully quiet. Stay overnight in Siruma so you can catch the sunrise up top!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months; sunrise or late afternoon.

places.name: Dalitiwan Resort and Sprite Falls
places.description: Ice-cold river pools in Majayjay! Dalitiwan Resort sits right along the national road in Majayjay, with a river-fed pool, natural rock pools and cottages under the trees, made for big family and group days. Just a few meters away, Sprite Falls has its own gate and a pretty cascade. Bring food to grill, come early for the best cottage, and wear aqua shoes because the stones are mossy!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season; weekday mornings for the best cottages.

places.name: Daraga Church
places.description: A church with a front-row view of Mayon! Daraga Church, officially the Church of Nuestra Señora de la Porteria, was built by the Franciscans in 1773 on a hilltop in Daraga, overlooking the sea and Mayon Volcano. Its Baroque facade of volcanic stone from Mayon is covered in intricate carvings, and the church is a National Cultural Treasure. Climb the steps, admire the details, then snap the classic church-and-volcano photo. Go early in the morning, when Mayon is clearest.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for clear Mayon views; drier months around March to May

places.name: Daranak Falls
places.description: Cool off in Rizal's favorite falls! Daranak Falls is a wide curtain of water dropping into a big, cool basin, just a short walk from the road in Tanay. It's one of the best-known nature spots in Rizal and a classic family and friends outing from Metro Manila, with picnic cottages and simple food stalls around the pool. Smaller Batlag Falls is a 10- to 15-minute walk away if you want a second stop. Come on a weekday morning in the dry season, March to May, for clearer water.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; dry season (March-May) for clearer water

places.name: Diniwid Beach
places.description: Boracay beauty, minus the crowds! Diniwid Beach is a small cove just north of White Beach Station 1, reached by a footpath that winds around the rocky headland. The sand is the same fine white and the water just as clear, with a fraction of the people. A few relaxed bars and boutique resorts line the shore, the swimming is calm, and it faces west for sunset. Walk over in the afternoon, swim, and stay for the golden hour.
places.best_time_to_visit: Afternoon to sunset, dry season

places.name: Donsol Whale Shark (Butanding) Interaction
places.description: Swim next to the biggest fish in the world: a true bucket-list moment! Donsol in Sorsogon is famous for its butanding, gentle whale sharks that feed in the bay during the season. Register at the Visitor Center in Dancalan, watch the short briefing, then head out on a boat with a trained Butanding Interaction Officer (BIO) who spots the sharks and guides you in. It's snorkeling only, and sightings depend on the day. Go between February and May for the best chances, and keep a spare day for the weather.
places.best_time_to_visit: February to May peak; season usually November to early June

places.name: Dumaluan Beach
places.description: Want Panglao's powdery white sand without the Alona crowds? Head to Dumaluan! This long, tree-lined beach on the island's south coast has fine white sand and clear, shallow turquoise water. Spread out in the shade, wade in at golden hour, and grab a meal at one of the beach resorts behind the shore. Come on a weekday morning for the emptiest stretch.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for the quietest stretch; low tide for long walks in the shallows.

places.name: Dupinga River
places.description: Cold, clear mountain water rushing past grassy Sierra Madre slopes! Dupinga River in Gabaldon is Nueva Ecija's favorite river day trip, with wide rocky banks, bamboo huts and plenty of shallow spots to sit in the current. It's the bigger, busier sister of nearby Calabasa River, less than 5 km away. Come on a dry-season weekday morning for clear water and a quiet bank, bring aqua shoes for the slippery rocks, and leave the moment the water turns brown!
places.best_time_to_visit: December to May, in the dry season. Avoid typhoon season, especially July to October.

places.name: Eden Nature Park
places.description: Pine trees, cool mountain air and a sky ride over the forest: Eden Nature Park is Davao's favorite escape from the city heat! Set on about 80 hectares in the hills of Toril, it mixes gardens and trails with adventure rides like the Skyrider, Skycycle and the 95-foot Skyswing. Take the guided shuttle tour around the property, visit the butterfly garden and Tinubdan cultural park, then have lunch with the view. Come in the morning and bring a light jacket.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning to early afternoon (open daily, 9am-5pm for day guests)

places.name: El Nido Island Hopping Tour A (Big Lagoon, Small Lagoon, Secret Lagoon)
places.description: El Nido's most famous tour! Tour A takes your bangka (outrigger boat) through Bacuit Bay's towering limestone cliffs to the famous lagoons of Miniloc Island: kayak into the emerald Big Lagoon, swim or kayak through the narrow gap of Small Lagoon, and squeeze through a hole in the rock into the tiny Secret Lagoon. Lunch is a seafood spread on the beach, with snorkeling stops along the way. Start early to beat the boats, bring a dry bag and wear aqua shoes.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May (dry season); early morning start

places.name: El Nido Island Hopping Tour B (Entalula, Snake Island, Cudugnon Cave)
places.description: Caves, sandbars and a world-famous beach! El Nido's Tour B is the quieter island-hopping route, built around Entalula Beach (one of the World's Top 50 Beaches in 2024), the sandbar of Snake Island, and the caves of Cudugnon and Cathedral Cave. A buffet lunch is included, and you are back in town by about 4 PM. It skips the big lagoons of Tour A, so it is perfect once you have done the classic route. Bring cash for the ₱400 eco-fee, which covers all your El Nido tours for 10 days!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months for calm seas; tours are cancelled when the weather turns.

places.name: El Nido Island Hopping Tour C (Hidden Beach, Secret Beach, Matinloc Shrine)
places.description: The wilder, more adventurous El Nido tour, and many groups' favorite day! Tour C heads to the outer islands of Bacuit Bay: Hidden Beach tucked behind towering limestone cliffs, Secret Beach reached by swimming through a small gap in the rock, and the abandoned Matinloc Shrine with a viewpoint over the cliffs, plus snorkeling at Helicopter Island. The open sea means it gets cancelled on rough days, so go in the calmer months and keep a spare day.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for the calmest seas

places.name: Enchanted Kingdom
places.description: Scream, laugh and ride all day at Enchanted Kingdom, the country's classic theme park, going strong since 1995! Brave the Space Shuttle loop, get soaked on Rio Grande rapids, and catch the city lights from the Wheel of Fate. Thrill-seekers should try EKlipse, a near-miss ride billed as the first of its kind in Southeast Asia, while Agila takes you soaring over Philippine landscapes in a flying theater. A day pass gives unlimited rides, and weekdays are cheaper and less crowded. The park opens at 11 AM and runs until 8 PM, so stay for the night lights. Leave your snacks at home, because outside food is not allowed!
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekdays (Wed-Fri) for shorter lines and lower rates; late afternoon into evening for cooler air and lights. In October 2026 the park is closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

places.name: Esmeris Farm (Daang Hari Campgrounds)
places.description: Front-row seats to a golden sunset for only ₱50! Esmeris Farm, home of the Daang Hari Campgrounds, is a family-run farm on the slopes of Mount Banahaw in Liliw, Laguna. Bamboo view decks and stilt huts perch on the edge of the hill, and Bali-style swings hang over the green valley. Grab a meal at the farm-to-table restaurant, nap in a hammock, then stay for the sunset, or camp overnight and wake up for sunrise. Make a full day of it and go shoe shopping in Liliw town too!
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon for the sunset; early morning for sunrise if you camp.

places.name: Forest Camp
places.description: A jungle hideaway just outside Dumaguete! Forest Camp in Valencia is a nature resort of cold, crystal-clear spring pools fed by mountain water, tucked under tall trees. Hop between the pools, cross the hanging bridge, ride the zipline over the stream, or walk the forest trails, then settle into a riverside hut for lunch. Come on a weekday morning for the quietest pools.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings; skip the day after heavy rain.

places.name: Fort Pilar Shrine and Museum
places.description: The historic heart of Zamboanga! The city traces its roots to the laying of Fort Pilar's first cornerstone on June 23, 1635. Today it's two places in one: on the outer wall is the open-air shrine of Our Lady of the Pillar, the city's patroness, where devotees light candles day and night, and inside the old Spanish fortress walls is a regional branch of the National Museum. Walk the courtyard and ramparts, then stroll to Paseo del Mar for sunset.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon, then sunset at Paseo del Mar

places.name: Fort Santiago
places.description: Walls, dungeons, river views and Rizal's last days: Fort Santiago is where Manila's history gets real! The Spanish-era fort guards the mouth of the Pasig River at the northern tip of Intramuros. Walk the Baluarte de Santa Barbara for river views, see the dungeons where prisoners were held during World War II, and visit the Rizal Shrine, where the national hero was imprisoned before his execution. It's a National Cultural Treasure. Go early in the morning or late afternoon to beat the heat.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekend early mornings (opens 6 AM) or late afternoon; Dec-Feb for cooler weather

places.description: Greek-style pillars on a cliff above a turquoise sea: Fortune Island is Batangas' Acropolis moment! The island once hosted a resort club that was later abandoned, and what remains is a photogenic mix of columns, ruins, white sand and clear coves. Climb up for the famous pillar photo, then swim and snorkel. There are almost no facilities, so pack food and lots of water. Go on a calm dry-season day.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (around Nov-May) on calm-sea days

places.name: Gallery by Chele
places.description: A Michelin-starred journey through Philippine ingredients, five floors above BGC. Gallery by Chele, led by Spanish-born chef Chele Gonzalez and chef Carlos Villaflor, sources about 90% of its ingredients locally from farmers, fishers and indigenous communities, grows endemic herbs in its own urban garden, and works with IRRI to bring back heirloom rice. There is no à la carte: choose a lunch set, or a six- or ten-course tasting menu in vegetarian or fish-and-meat versions. Each course is a story about a place or tradition, plated like art. Save it for an anniversary or a big treat. Book directly by email or phone, and tell them about allergies ahead.
places.best_time_to_visit: Friday or Saturday dinner, or Wednesday-Sunday lunch; closed Mondays

places.name: Garin Farm Pilgrimage Resort
places.description: Climb all the way to 'heaven on earth'! At Garin Farm in San Joaquin, the famous Stairway to Heaven, 480 steps, passes life-size scenes from the life of Jesus, then a dark tunnel opens onto a dazzling all-white world of angels and clouds under a giant cross. It really does feel unreal! Down below there are farm activities, ziplining and fishing, and rooms if you want to stay the night. Go early, and bring sunglasses: all that white glows in the sun.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning or late afternoon; the white area is very bright and hot at midday.

places.name: Good Shepherd Convent
places.description: The food-gift stop you can't skip! The Religious of the Good Shepherd make the famous Mountain Maid ube jam, plus strawberry jam, peanut brittle, lengua de gato and choco crinkles. Every purchase helps fund education for youth from the Cordilleras. Ube jam is limited to two bottles per person and sells out, so come early on a weekday. Enjoy the view from the deck, then walk down to Mines View Park.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings, right after opening

places.name: Guimaras Island Hopping (Alubihod Beach)
places.description: Sweet mangoes, white coves and a short boat ride from Iloilo: Guimaras is the easiest island escape in Western Visayas! Cross from Iloilo, head to Alubihod Beach in Nueva Valencia, then hire a bangka to hop around Ave Maria Islet, Natago Beach, Baras Cave and other little coves. Swim, snorkel and feast on fresh mangoes before heading back. Come in April or May for mango season and the Manggahan Festival.
places.best_time_to_visit: April to May for mango season and the Manggahan Festival

places.name: Guisi Lighthouse and Beach
places.description: Rusty Spanish-era lighthouse ruins on a jungle hill, with a quiet cove of clear water right below: Guisi is Guimaras at its most cinematic! Walk around the old iron tower and the vine-covered stone walls, then head down for a swim at Guisi Beach. It is a regular stop on Guimaras day tours with the Trappist Monastery and Alubihod, so pair them in one easy loop from Iloilo.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season mornings for clear water and softer light on the ruins.

places.name: Halo-Halo de Iloko
places.description: Halo-halo worthy of a museum! Halo-Halo de Iloko is an ancestral house in San Fernando, La Union turned restaurant-museum, filled wall to wall with antiques and vintage finds. The star is the creative halo-halo: try the famous fried halo-halo, wrapped in lumpia wrapper and topped with ice cream, ube and cheese, or the buko (young coconut) halo-halo. Stay for a real Ilocano meal too, like emparedados with La Union longganisa and okoy with their sweet-tangy vinegar. A worthy detour to or from the San Juan surf beaches, especially on a hot afternoon.
places.best_time_to_visit: Hot afternoons, for a cold snack

places.name: Hapao Rice Terraces
places.description: A whole valley of UNESCO rice terraces, and you can see it straight from the road! Hapao, at the Banaue end of Hungduan, is one of the five Ifugao terrace clusters on the UNESCO World Heritage list, with paddies stepping down to the Hapao River. Walk the terrace walls past village houses, then follow the trail to Boyah (Bogyah) Hot Spring, where 39 to 41 degree water bubbles up right beside the cold river. Come April or May when the fields are at their greenest, or around July and August when they turn gold for harvest. Stay overnight in a local homestay for misty mornings, and bring cash, because there's no ATM in town!
places.best_time_to_visit: April to May for the greenest terraces; July to August for golden harvest fields. Dry months (December to June) are easiest on the roads.

places.name: Helm by Josh Boutwood
places.description: The Philippines' only two-Michelin-star restaurant: Helm is the big-celebration splurge every foodie dreams about! Chef Josh Boutwood serves themed, seasonal set menus that change through the year, and the open kitchen turns dinner into a show: you watch every dish being built, and the chefs talk to you directly. Expect intricate plating, bold flavor pairings and polished service. The setting is very intimate, so it's a top pick for an anniversary or a proposal. It's on the 3rd floor of The Shops at Ayala Triangle Gardens. Book well ahead, since slots go fast.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dinner, Tuesday to Sunday; lunch Friday to Sunday

places.name: Hidden Valley Springs
places.description: A jungle full of warm and cool spring pools! Hidden Valley Springs is a rainforest resort in Laguna, where about seven natural pools at different temperatures are scattered under giant ferns and palms, some with little cascades to sit under. A short trail leads to a hidden waterfall at the end, and a Filipino buffet lunch is part of the day tour. It is about 1.5 to 2 hours from Manila, so it makes a dreamy day trip. Book ahead!
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekdays all year; the dry season is best for the falls trail.

places.name: Hinagdanan Cave
places.description: A cave with its own lagoon! Hinagdanan Cave on Panglao was found by accident when the landowner threw a stone into a hole and heard a splash; the name comes from 'hagdan' (ladder), since ladders were once used to get inside. Today, steps lead down into a naturally lit cavern with big stalactites and stalagmites over a deep lagoon. Go late in the morning, when sunbeams shine through the holes in the ceiling.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late morning, when sunlight shines through the ceiling holes

places.name: Enchanted River (Hinatuan)
places.description: A river so blue that locals say it's guarded by spirits! The Enchanted River in Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur glows sapphire and jade, and its depth is still a mystery to many. The main pool is for sightseeing only, but there's a designated swimming area nearby, with life vests for rent. Catch the daily fish feeding, take photos from the banks, then pair it with Tinuy-an Falls in Bislig. Go on a weekday in the dry season for the clearest water.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekdays in the dry season, for the clearest water and fewer crowds

places.name: Hinulugang Taktak Nature and Adventure Park
places.description: Antipolo's legendary waterfall is back in the spotlight! Hinulugang Taktak was declared a national park in 1990, and today it is a free nature and adventure park right at the edge of Metro Manila. Walk the canopy zone's hanging bridges, try wall climbing, cool off in the swimming pool, or lie on the spider web net hanging right above the 21-meter falls for a wild photo! There are gazebos and picnic tables for a lazy family afternoon too. A new sewage treatment plant opened in late 2025 to clean up the river that feeds the falls. Tip: wear rubber shoes with laces for the adventure zone, since Crocs are not allowed, and remember activities are for ages 14 and up.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings for fewer people; the rainy months (June-October) give the strongest water flow. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Honda Bay Island Hopping
places.description: Island hopping without going far from the city! Honda Bay is about 25 minutes from Puerto Princesa, and from Sta. Lourdes wharf, pumpboats take you to small islands with white sandbars and clear water. Spot starfish on Starfish Island, swim on Luli Island's sandbar, snorkel at the reef and have lunch on Cowrie Island. Calm, shallow water makes it great for families. Go on a dry-season morning.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season (around November to May), morning

places.name: Hulugan Falls
places.description: Get ready to feel the mist! Hulugan Falls drops about 70 meters down a mossy rock wall in the forests of Luisiana, and it is one of the most jaw-dropping waterfalls near Manila. The trek from the Captain's House jump-off takes 45 minutes to an hour, with an easier long trail or a steep, slippery shortcut. Your local guide can also lead you to neighboring Talay Falls and Hidden Falls, so you can chase three waterfalls in one day! Rent a life vest, cool off in the basin, and take that dreamy photo in the spray. Fees are cheap, but bring cash because there are no ATMs or GCash at the site. Tip: wear shoes with real grip and pack a waterproof bag for your phone.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, December to February, for cooler weather and safer trails. Weekdays for fewer people. In the rainy season (June-November) the trail is sometimes closed for safety.

places.name: Hundred Islands National Park
places.description: A bay full of limestone islands and one of the easiest island-hopping trips from Manila! Boats leave from Lucap Wharf in Alaminos. The developed islands are Quezon, Governor's, Children's and Pilgrimage Island, topped by a giant Christ the Savior statue. Climb the Governor's Island view deck for the classic photo, snorkel and kayak around the coves, and peek into Imelda Cave on Marcos Island. Bring your own food and water, use reef-safe sunscreen and take all trash back. Rent a full-day boat as a group of five to split the cost, and go on a weekday to skip the crowds.
places.best_time_to_visit: December to May (dry season); weekdays, early morning departure

places.name: Igorot Stone Kingdom
places.description: Great Wall vibes in Baguio! Igorot Stone Kingdom is a stone park of towers, terraces, bridges and stairways built with stone-layered riprap walls that celebrate Igorot heritage. It opened in 2021 and went viral for its fortress look, with figures inspired by Igorot mythology. Climb the ramparts, pose in rented Cordillera attire and take in the hillside views. It's a modern photo park rather than a historic site, but it's fun for families and friends. Pair it with Tam-awan Village nearby.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon on clear, dry days

places.name: Imelda's Garden
places.description: Taal Lake like you have never seen it! Imelda's Garden spills down a steep hillside in Cuenca, on the opposite shore from Tagaytay, so you get a big, open view of the lake and Volcano Island, plus Mt. Maculot right behind you. Walkways zigzag through themed flower gardens with swings, gazebos, pergolas and a rainbow arch made for photos, and the Tanaw Café and food kiosks keep you fed. A local named Antonio Mendoza built it over three years and named it after his wife. Go in the morning for clear skies and soft light!
places.best_time_to_visit: Cool, clear mornings from November to February; weekdays are quieter.

places.name: Inatô
places.description: Eight seats, one marble counter and Filipino food cooked 'our way': that's Inatô, Chef JP Cruz's one-Michelin-star gem tucked in The Alley at Karrivin. The name is Binisaya for 'our way', and the seasonal menu reworks Filipino flavors and cooking techniques with local and global ingredients. Michelin calls out the yellowtail amberjack and the choco tarte. You sit right in front of the open kitchen, so it feels like a secret dinner party: quiet, intimate and personal. Book it for a special date. There are only two counter seatings a night, 6 PM and 8:30 PM, so book early.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dinner, Tuesday to Saturday (6 PM or 8:30 PM seating)

places.name: Infinity Farm
places.description: Cold, fast rapids straight from Mt. Halcon! Infinity Farm is a farm resort in Baco where a crystal-clear mountain river tumbles over boulders into turquoise pools, with tables set right by the water. Pick a spot along the river, wade into the natural pools and let the current cool you down. It is open on weekends only and all bookings are online, so plan ahead. A Mindoro road-trip must!
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekend mornings in the dry months (March to May).

opening_hours.note: Day tours only; last admission 3 PM

places.name: Intramuros
places.description: A whole walled city, not just one tourist spot! Intramuros was the heart of Spanish Manila, ringed by thick stone walls and bastions. World War II flattened much of it, but San Agustin Church, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, still stands, and much of the walled city has been rebuilt. Walk the cobblestone streets, explore Fort Santiago and the Rizal Shrine, step inside Casa Manila and Manila Cathedral, and ride a bike or kalesa between the gates. Pick two or three anchors instead of rushing everything. Spend the morning in museums, then take a slow sunset walk on the walls.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning for museums; late afternoon to sunset for the walls

places.name: Islas de Gigantes
places.description: Unlimited scallops, limestone islets and a lagoon hidden inside cliffs: Islas de Gigantes is the big group island adventure in northern Iloilo! The islands sit in the Visayan Sea off Carles. Hike up the viewpoint on Cabugao Gamay for the famous shot of its white beach and rocky hill, swim in Tangke, a saltwater lagoon walled by cliffs, and feast on famously cheap scallops. The boat ride is long, so stay at least one night. Go from March to May, when the sea is calmer and the water clearest.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for calm seas

places.name: Itbayat Island
places.description: The last frontier of Batanes, the northernmost town in the Philippines and closer to Taiwan than to mainland Luzon! Itbayat is a giant uplifted coral island ringed by sheer cliffs, and only a few travelers make it here each year. Walk out to Rapang Cliff with its mushroom-shaped rocks and bonsai-like trees, climb Mt. Karoboboan for a view of the whole island, and step into Torongan Cave, believed to be where the first Austronesian settlers landed. Getting here is part of the adventure: a bumpy faluwa ride or a tiny plane from Basco!
places.best_time_to_visit: Outside the windy December to February months and typhoon season; boats and flights stop whenever the sea or weather turns bad.

places.name: Jomalig Island and Salibungot Beach
places.description: Jomalig is the golden island of Quezon, and Salibungot Beach is why people make the long trip! Its deep amber sand glows orange in the late afternoon, framed by a line of shady agoho trees and the open Pacific. Ride a habal-habal around the island to Little Boracay for calm swimming, the cliffs of Lingayen Cove, nicknamed Little Batanes, and the lone bent tree at Kanaway Beach. Island-hop to sandbars and rocky islets, then feast on a cook-to-order seafood dinner at your resort. This is a real adventure: an overnight bus to Real and a five-hour boat ride. Bring small bills, a power bank and a dry bag, and book your resort first.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for the calmest crossing; November to May is the safe window. Avoid June to October (Habagat and typhoon season).

places.name: Jones Bridge
places.description: Manila's prettiest bridge, with Paris energy over the Pasig River! Restored to its old-world look with ornate lamp posts and graceful statues, Jones Bridge glows at blue hour, with views of the Manila Central Post Office, Binondo and the river all at once. It's a quick photo stop, not a hangout: snap your shots from the sidewalk, then walk on to Binondo for food or Escolta for old Manila buildings. Go at sunset, mind your bag and phone, and stay on the sidewalk.
places.best_time_to_visit: Sunset to blue hour, when the lamps turn on

places.name: Jovellar Underground River
places.description: Float through a mountain on a bamboo raft! At the Jovellar Underground River, a guide poles your raft through a lit limestone cave, and you come out into a deep gorge pool for swimming and cliff jumping, with a waterfall downstream. It is run by the town and costs very little, about an hour from Legazpi. Add dry caving if you want more adventure!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season mornings; skip it after heavy rain.

places.name: Kalanggaman Island
places.description: A sandbar so white and long it looks edited! Kalanggaman is the Leyte island that ranked 25th in The World's 50 Best Beaches 2026. Run by the Palompon local government, it sits offshore with sandbars trailing into turquoise water. There's no electricity and no hotel, just cottages, grills and restrooms, which keeps it clean and quiet. Walk the sandbar at low tide, snorkel the reef, grill your packed food and just stare at the colors. Go in the dry months for calm seas, leave Palompon early, and pack food, water and shade for the whole day.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May; low tide for the full sandbar

places.name: Kapangan Day Tour (Amburayan River and Ongong Falls)
places.description: Benguet's quiet waterfall town, just a couple of hours from Baguio! Kapangan day tours string together a swim in the wide, jade-green Amburayan River, a trek down to Ongong Falls and a climb up Mt. Kalukasog for big mountain views. Start at the municipal tourism office, where local guides are arranged, then spend the day hopping between river pools and falls. Come in the dry months, pack a change of clothes and wear shoes that can get wet!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, roughly December to May; start early so you finish the treks before afternoon rain.

places.name: Kapurpurawan Rock Formation
places.description: Brilliant white rocks by the sea! Kapurpurawan in Burgos, Ilocos Norte is a cluster of creamy white rock formations sculpted by wind, water and waves into soft, wavy shapes facing the wild sea. The name comes from the Ilocano word 'puraw', meaning white. From the drop-off, it's a short walk along the rocky shore, or you can ride a horse to the formations. Watch the waves crash, shoot the white rocks against a blue sky, then continue to Cape Bojeador Lighthouse and the Bangui windmills nearby. Go in the late afternoon for softer light and less heat.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon; dry season (November to May)

places.name: Kása Palma
places.description: A tropical beach house in the middle of Poblacion: Kása Palma is Chef Aaron Isip's one-Michelin-star restaurant, all straw cloche lamps, lush greenery and shell-lined walls. He blends French technique with Latin American and Southeast Asian flavors, cooking over wood fire with local ingredients. Choose a tasting menu on the breezy terrace, or go à la carte at the counter with a view of the open kitchen. The vibe is relaxed fine dining, laid-back but stylish, great for a date or a small celebration with friends. Dinner runs Tuesday to Saturday, so plan your special night around that.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dinner, Tuesday to Saturday

places.name: Katibawasan Falls
places.description: A slender ribbon of water dropping about 70 meters into an icy pool, framed by ferns: Katibawasan is Camiguin's most graceful waterfall! It sits at the foot of Mt. Timpoong, so the water is cold enough to wake you up after a hot day of island touring. The walk from the entrance is short and easy, with picnic tables nearby, so it's great for families and grandparents too. It's only about 5 km from Mambajao, so it fits nicely into a Camiguin loop with the Sunken Cemetery and hot springs. Go in the morning for softer light and a quieter pool.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning; dry months for the clearest pool

places.name: Katungkulan Beach (Marine Base Ternate)
places.description: Cavite's "Boracay"! Katungkulan Beach is a cove of soft, pale sand and clear water with a big green cliff at one end, and it sits inside a Philippine Marine base in Ternate. That means a gate, rules and a quiet, clean beach without the resort sprawl. Bring your own food, set up under the trees and swim the calm cove. Treat it as a day trip, go on a weekday morning, and you might have a whole stretch of sand to yourselves!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, March to May; weekday mornings.

places.name: Kawasan Falls
places.description: Milky turquoise pools and cool spring water: Kawasan is Cebu's most famous waterfall for a reason! It's a three-tier cascade in Badian, about a 1.5 km walk from the entrance to the first falls. Ride a bamboo raft right under the main falls, swim in the basins and eat at the riverside stalls after. Kawasan is also the grand finale of the Badian canyoneering trip, so expect excited groups jumping and sliding in from upriver. Arrive early in the morning, in the dry season, for clear water before the crowds. A worth-it side trip from Moalboal!
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning; dry season (around January to May) for the clearest water

places.name: Kaway'an EcoPark
places.description: Bamboo like you have never seen it! Kaway'an EcoPark is the only Philippine spot on TIME's World's Greatest Places 2026 list, and one look at the Marilag Grand Pavilion tells you why. Giant bamboo columns rise like a forest, and the curvy Marahuyo Bridge arches over a calm lagoon. Rent a boat, ride one of the gentle horses rescued after the 2020 Taal eruption, try fishing, or just spread a picnic mat on the lawns and chill. It is about 90 minutes from Manila, so it makes an easy day trip for families, couples and friends. Entry is only ₱150 for a full day! Come on a Friday or weekend for the 7 AM opening, when the light is soft and the bamboo glows. Remember, it is closed on Mondays.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, December to May. Come at opening (7 AM on Fridays, weekends and holidays) or late afternoon for soft light and cooler air. Closed Mondays.

opening_hours.note: Holidays 7 AM-7 PM; when Monday is a holiday it closes Tuesday instead

places.name: Kayangan Lake
places.description: Coron's signature shot, and a lake often called the cleanest in the Philippines! From the boat dock, climb the steep steps and pause at the famous viewpoint over the cove for that postcard photo, then head down to a crystal-clear lake ringed by limestone cliffs. The water is so clear you can see the rock formations below while floating. Kayangan is protected by the indigenous Tagbanua, so follow their rules. Life vests are required. Go early in the dry season to beat the tour-boat rush.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to May; arrive early before tour boats

places.name: Kayapa Trilogy and Quad Peak Hike
places.description: Grassy ridges, giant boulders and clouds racing over the Cordillera: Kayapa is a hiker's playground! The Kayapa Trilogy links Mt. Tugew, Mt. Cabo and Mt. Kabuan, three summits between about 1,320 and 1,460 MASL, on a roughly 12 km loop rated a minor 3/9. Want more? The Quad Peak route out of Alang-Salacsac adds a fourth summit. Expect open trails along rolling ridgelines, a big rock to scramble up for the money shot, and wide mountain views. A local guide is required, so book one at the jump-off or through a tour group, and pack sun protection: there's little shade up there!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, around November to May. Start early to beat the midday sun on the open ridges.

places.name: Kiltepan Viewpoint
places.description: Wake up early, it's worth it! Kiltepan is Sagada's most famous sunrise spot. Get there in the dark, find a spot on the rocks and wait as the sky turns orange over the Cordillera ridges. On lucky mornings, a thick sea of clouds fills the valley below while the rice terraces peek through. It's cold, so bring a jacket and grab hot coffee from the vendors. Clouds are never guaranteed, but the mountain view alone makes the early alarm worth it. Weekends and long holidays get packed, so a weekday sunrise is the dream.
places.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise (be there by around 5 AM); weekdays; cool months for better cloud chances

places.name: Kota Beach
places.description: Bantayan's postcard beach, like Boracay back in the day! Kota Beach in Santa Fe has powdery white sand, shallow turquoise water and a sandbar that stretches out at low tide, with a small rock islet you can wade to. There are only a few cottages and resorts here, so the vibe is slow: sunbathe, swim, float and do absolutely nothing with friends. Time your visit with low tide, stay for the sunset, then head back to Santa Fe town for grilled seafood and Bantayan's famous dried fish. Go in the dry months for the calmest, clearest water.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May; low tide for the sandbar

places.name: La Mesa Eco Park
places.description: Fresh air, big trees and birdsong, right in Quezon City! La Mesa Eco Park is a 33-hectare green escape at the edge of the La Mesa Watershed, the forest that protects one of Metro Manila's main water sources. Managed by the Manila Water Foundation, it's great for a nature walk, a family picnic or a morning of birdwatching without leaving the city. Follow the eco-trail under tall trees and look out over the lagoon. It's a protected watershed, not a swimming resort, so keep it clean and quiet. Come early on a weekday with water, insect repellent and comfy shoes.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings, before the midday heat; dry season Nov-May

places.name: La Trinidad Strawberry Farm
places.description: Strawberry picking, let's go! La Trinidad, right next to Baguio, is famous for its strawberries, and its valley farm is where visitors pick their own berries straight from the rows. During the cool months you fill a basket and pay by the kilo, then wander the stalls for strawberry taho, ice cream, jams, wine and fresh Benguet vegetables. It's touristy and can get muddy, but kids and first-timers love it, and the berries are as fresh as they get. Go in the morning during peak season and wear shoes you don't mind getting dirty.
places.best_time_to_visit: Mornings during peak season, around December to April

places.name: Laiya Beach
places.description: White sand, no flight needed! Laiya is the group and family beach escape on Batangas' eastern coast. This long stretch of fine, light sand in San Juan is lined with resorts from budget-friendly to upscale. In summer the water is calm and clear, good for swimming, kayaking and banana boat rides, and most resorts offer day-use passes if you only have one free day. Stay overnight for a proper weekend: grill by the beach, karaoke at night, sunrise swim in the morning. Go on a weekday or book early for summer weekends, when Laiya gets packed.
places.best_time_to_visit: March-May for calm water; weekdays for fewer crowds

places.name: Lakawon Island
places.description: White sand, clear shallow water and a relaxed group vibe: Lakawon is Negros Occidental's favorite island day out! The island sits a short boat ride off Cadiz, and its long, curving beach is made for lazy swims and kayak paddles. The resort is known for its floating bar, so a drink over the water is part of the fun. Day trips from Bacolod are easy, and there are cottages if you want to sleep over and catch the morning calm. Go on a weekday in the dry months, when the water is clearest and the beach quieter.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May; weekdays

places.name: Lake Danao Natural Park
places.description: Lake Danao is Ormoc's cool-air escape: a 148-hectare, guitar-shaped volcanic lake about 650–700 m above sea level, ringed by forested mountains. It reopened in late August 2026 after almost 11 months of rehabilitation, so kayaks, paddle boats and local bancas are back on the water. Paddle out early when the lake is glass-still and misty, walk the perimeter trails, and bring binoculars: the natural park has 84 recorded bird species. Food vendors sit by the shore, but pack a light jacket; it is noticeably cooler than the city. Follow the park's no-litter rules to keep the water clean.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning for mist and calm water; dry months for the trails.

places.name: Las Cabanas Beach
places.description: El Nido's favorite sunset spot, a short tricycle ride south of town! Las Cabanas is a white-sand beach with clear water facing Bacuit Bay, lined with laid-back beach bars. Grab a beanbag and a cold drink, swim while the sun is still up, then watch it sink behind the islands in a burst of orange. It's lively but relaxed, great for friends or a date night after a day of island hopping. Arrive by around 4:30 PM for a good spot, and arrange your ride back to town before dark.
places.best_time_to_visit: About 4:30pm to sunset, dry season (November-May)

places.name: Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar
places.description: Time travel in Bataan! Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar is a heritage resort where Spanish-colonial stone houses from across Luzon were taken apart and rebuilt brick by brick into a riverside town of cobblestone streets. Join the guided heritage walking tour, ride a balsa raft on the river, dress up in Filipiniana for photos, then cool off at the beach or pool. Staying overnight in a restored casa is the full experience, and it was named Best Historic Hotel in Asia and the Pacific in 2021. Moving the houses is debated by conservationists, but it's one of the most immersive history trips near Manila. Go at golden hour, when the old houses glow.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season weekdays; late afternoon for photos

places.name: Lazi Church and Convent
places.description: A heritage stop that's worth it on any Siquijor loop! The San Isidro Labrador Church in Lazi is built of sea stones and hardwood, with its old retablo, two pulpits and wooden floors still in place. Across the road stands the huge convent, now home to the Siquijor Heritage Museum. Walk the creaky floors, admire the craftsmanship, then head to Cambugahay Falls nearby.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning, combined with Cambugahay Falls

places.name: Leslie's
places.description: Hot bulalo, cool air and Taal Volcano in front of you: Leslie's is the classic Tagaytay lunch! This long-running ridge restaurant beside Sky Ranch serves the dishes Tagaytay is famous for, in open, nipa-style dining areas facing the lake and volcano. Order a big pot of bulalo to share, crispy tawilis (a small Taal Lake fish), sinigang and grilled liempo. It's busy and no-frills, but hot soup, cool air and that view are exactly what a Tagaytay road trip is about. Go on a clear day, then walk over to Sky Ranch.
places.best_time_to_visit: Lunch on a clear day; weekdays to avoid long waits

places.name: Ligñon Hill Nature Park
places.description: Want Mayon right in front of you? Head up Ligñon Hill! This hill on Legazpi's edge has a nature park at the top with a view deck facing Mayon Volcano head-on, plus the city and Albay Gulf below. Walk or ride up the spiral road, then explore the old Japanese tunnel, a zipline for the brave, cafes and souvenir shops. It's the city's favorite sunrise and sunset hangout, and an easy first stop to get your bearings. Go early in the morning, when Mayon is most likely to show its perfect cone before the clouds roll in.
places.best_time_to_visit: Sunrise or late afternoon; early morning for the clearest Mayon view

opening_hours.note: Hours might differ; park being redeveloped, some attractions may be closed

places.name: Limasawa Island
places.description: Sail to where Christianity in the Philippines began! Limasawa, a small green island off Southern Leyte, is where the first Easter Sunday Mass in the country was held on March 31, 1521. Visit the First Mass Shrine and the cross on the hill, then swim and snorkel in clear water over coral reefs. Stay a night in one of the small resorts to enjoy the island once the day-trippers leave.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season for calmer seas; around March 31 for the First Mass anniversary.

places.name: Linapacan Islands (Araw Beach)
places.description: The quiet islands between El Nido and Coron! Linapacan is a whole town of small islands with fine white sand, and its water is so clear it has landed on lists of the clearest seas in the world. Creators rank Araw Beach among the best beaches in all of Palawan, yet you will share it with only a few other boats. There are no big resorts and no ATMs here, so it is pure island life: camp on a beach, snorkel over the reefs and hop between empty islands. It takes effort to get here, which is exactly why it still feels so empty!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, roughly December to May, when the sea is calm enough for long boat rides.

places.name: Lio Beach
places.description: Clean white sand, calm water and sunsets made for slow evenings! Lio Beach is a long, wide stretch on El Nido's northern coast inside Ayala Land's planned Lio Tourism Estate, just minutes from the airport. The beach is open to everyone, with cafes, shops and restaurants a short walk from the sand. It is only a 10 to 15 minute tricycle ride from El Nido town, so come in the late afternoon, rent a sunbed, swim, and stay for the sunset. If you want a calmer break from the town buzz, this is it!
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon into sunset.

places.name: Little Boracay Sandbar (Calatagan)
places.description: Grill seafood on a floating bamboo cottage, then wade out to a white sandbar in the middle of the sea! Little Boracay is Calatagan's famous low-tide sandbar, about 115 km south of Metro Manila. It is not a separate island: the sand only rises above the water at low tide, so timing is everything. From November to March, low tide falls in the morning; from April it shifts to the late afternoon. Rent a balsa (floating cottage) with your group, buy your seafood at the Calatagan Public Market on the way, and float the day away. Check the PAGASA tide table before you pick your date!
places.best_time_to_visit: December to May for calm, sunny days. Plan your boat around low tide: mornings from November to March, late afternoon from April.

places.name: Loboc River Cruise
places.description: Lunch on a floating restaurant while emerald water and coconut palms drift by: the Loboc River cruise is the relaxing lunch break of every Bohol countryside tour! You board a covered raft with a Filipino buffet and live acoustic music, then glide upriver, stopping at a floating stage where locals sing and dance. The town's old church sits right by the river. It suits families with grandparents, or anyone who wants a relaxed, scenic lunch between the Chocolate Hills and the tarsiers.
places.best_time_to_visit: Lunchtime, as part of a countryside tour

places.name: Lucban Town and Pahiyas Streets
places.description: The most colorful town in the country every May 15! Lucban, a cool town at the foot of Mt. Banahaw in Quezon, celebrates the Pahiyas Festival for San Isidro Labrador, patron of farmers, by covering houses in kiping (colorful rice wafers), fruits and vegetables. Even outside May, it's a worth-it food trip: slurp pancit habhab straight off a banana leaf, buy garlicky Lucban longganisa, and visit the San Luis Obispo de Tolosa Church and the Kamay ni Hesus shrine. Buddy's is the classic stop for habhab and longganisa. For Pahiyas, come early in the morning before the crowds.
places.best_time_to_visit: May 15 for Pahiyas (go early); cool weekdays for the food trip

places.name: Luna Pebble Beach and Baluarte Watchtower
places.description: A beach with no sand at all, just a shore of smooth, round pebbles! Luna's pebble beach runs along the coast of La Union, and right on it stands the Baluarte, a 400-year-old Spanish-era watchtower that once kept watch for pirates. Step inside the restored tower, listen to the waves rattle the stones and stay for the sunset over the West Philippine Sea. Swimming is not allowed here, so come for the views, the history and the photos!
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon for the sunset, especially in the dry months from November to May.

places.name: Luzon Datum of 1911 and Balanacan View Deck
places.description: Stand on the exact spot that is the zero point for every map in the Philippines! The Luzon Datum of 1911 is a small marker on a hill above Balanacan Port, and it is why Marinduque is called the Heart of the Philippines. Walk up the steps for wide views of Balanacan Bay and the sea, and drop by the view deck near the port for photos. It is quick and easy to combine with your ferry arrival or the island loop. Tip: climb in the early morning or late afternoon when it is cooler, and ask the caretaker at the site for the story behind the marker.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning or late afternoon; dry months November to June.

places.name: Ma-Cho Temple
places.description: Red pillars, golden dragons and a sea view: Ma-Cho Temple is La Union's most striking photo stop! Construction of this Taoist temple on a hill in San Fernando began in 1975, honoring Mazu (Ma-Cho), the sea goddess who protects sailors. Walk through the grand gate, past the bamboo garden, ponds and pagoda, then look out over the city and the sea. It's an active place of worship, so keep your voice down and dress modestly. It fits easily into a morning before heading to the beaches of San Juan.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon; September for Mazu's feast

places.name: Maasin River
places.description: Green water, coconut palms and a rope swing: Maasin River is the relaxing swimming stop on every Siargao land tour! The calm river runs under the Maasin Bridge in General Luna, lined with palms and mangroves. It became famous for a bent coconut tree with a rope swing; that tree died in 2023, but the swings and jumps carry on. Swing, splash, then rent a small boat or kayak and paddle upstream into the quiet palm-lined bends. Pair it with the coconut road viewpoints on the same ride, in the morning or late afternoon.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning or late afternoon

places.name: Mactan Island Hopping (Nalusuan, Hilutungan, Pandanon)
places.description: The easiest beach-and-snorkel day from Metro Cebu! Bangkas (outrigger boats) leave from Mactan for the Olango island group, where marine sanctuaries like Hilutungan and Nalusuan have fish swarming around you in clear, shallow water. Then it's off to a sandbar island like Pandanon or Caohagan for a seafood barbecue lunch on the sand. Bring an underwater camera; the fish come close! Calm and family-friendly, it's ideal if you're staying in the city or at a Mactan resort. Go on a dry-season morning for the calmest water.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May, mornings

places.name: Magalawa Island
places.description: Powdery white sand curling into a long sandbar, with clear blue water on both sides: Magalawa is Palauig's own little Boracay! The island is just a 10 to 15 minute boat ride from the Palauig coast, and it's lined with shady trees, simple beach resorts and campsites. Walk the sandbar, swim in the calm shallows, and stay for the sunrise over the Zambales mountains. Book with a known resort for your boat and cottage, and keep an eye on the currents!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, around November to May. Sunrise and early morning for the softest light.

places.name: Magpupungko Rock Pools
places.description: Crystal-clear lagoons that only appear when the sea pulls back: Magpupungko is Siargao's most magical low-tide stop! On the east coast in Pilar, the receding tide reveals natural pools in the flat reef, clear enough to see every rock below. Swim, float and take turns doing small jumps into the deeper parts, then rest on the long white beach beside it. At high tide the pools vanish under the waves, so arrive about an hour before low tide, when they're fully open.
places.best_time_to_visit: Low tide only; calm-sea days in the drier months

places.name: Malacañang of the North
places.description: A presidential mansion on the shore of Paoay Lake: whatever your take on history, Malacañang of the North is a big stop in Ilocos Norte. The two-story house of the Marcos family, with capiz windows, wide hardwood floors and a veranda overlooking the lake, is now a museum run by the provincial government. Inside are themed rooms with period furniture, photos and memorabilia. Step out to the veranda and lakeside lawns for the view. Most South Ilocos Norte day tours bundle it with Paoay Church and the sand dunes.
places.best_time_to_visit: Daytime; morning for cooler weather

places.name: Malagos Garden Resort
places.description: Davao's favourite garden day out! Malagos Garden Resort in the uplands of Baguio District is a leafy world of gardens and aviaries, where colourful lovebirds hop right onto your hands in the bird-feeding dome. Then step into the Malagos Chocolate Museum, the first chocolate museum in the country, and learn how Davao cacao becomes award-winning chocolate. Come in the morning while it's cool.
places.best_time_to_visit: Mornings, while the air is cool.

places.name: Malapascua Thresher Shark Dive (Monad Shoal)
places.description: Wake up before sunrise for one of diving's most special sights: thresher sharks with their long, whip-like tails, circling a reef near you! Monad Shoal near Malapascua is famous for regular thresher sightings at dawn. It's a deep dive, so you need to be certified, and Advanced is recommended. Not certified yet? Malapascua's dive shops run courses, so you can learn and see them on the same trip. Stay a few nights and add Gato Island or the island's white beaches.
places.best_time_to_visit: Year-round; dawn dives give the best chance

places.name: Malcapuya Island (Coron Island Escapade)
places.description: White sand worthy of Boracay, minus the crowds! The Coron Island Escapade tour trades lakes and lagoons for pure beach days: Malcapuya Island's powdery white sand and clear water, plus Banana Island and the Bulog Dos sandbar, a long boat ride from Coron town. Swim, snorkel, relax under the trees and eat a grilled lunch on the sand. Less cliff drama, more classic Palawan postcard, great for families and friends who want to beach all day. Go on a calm day between March and May, when the sea is glassy.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for calm seas

places.name: Malico: Mt. Malico Camping and Falls
places.description: Pine forest, cold air and a campfire under the stars: Malico is Pangasinan's mountain hideaway! This highland barangay of San Nicolas, ancestral home of the Kalanguya, sits at the foot of Mt. Malico along the zigzag Villa Verde Trail. Pitch a tent or book an A-frame cabin at a farm campsite, watch the city lights from the ridge at night, and chase the small waterfalls tucked in the forest nearby. Pangasinan even named it its summer capital barangay. Bring a jacket, because evenings get properly cold!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry months, around November to May. Late afternoon to sunset is when it starts to get cold and cozy.

places.name: Maligcong Rice Terraces and Mt. Kupapey Sunrise
places.description: Stone-walled rice terraces rising like a giant amphitheatre, and you get them almost to yourself! Maligcong, a quiet village 30 minutes above Bontoc town, is now a declared National Cultural Treasure. The move here is a 3:30 AM hike up Mt. Kupapey (also spelled Kofafey, 1,647 MASL, beginner-friendly at 3/9). You reach the summit in about 1.5-2 hours, in time for sunrise over the terraces, and on lucky December mornings a sea of clouds. After that, walk down through the paddies, sip tea on a homestay veranda, and climb Mt. Fato in the afternoon if you still have legs. Hire a local guide because the trail is easy to lose in the dark, bring a jacket, and carry cash because there's no ATM in Maligcong.
places.best_time_to_visit: May to July for the greenest terraces (planting starts in April, harvest is in August). December has the best chance of a sea of clouds at sunrise. Start the Kupapey hike around 3:30 AM to catch sunrise.

places.name: Malumpati Cold Spring
places.description: That electric-blue water is real, and it's cold! Malumpati Cold Spring in Pandan, Antique is a forest-shaded natural pool, about 40 metres long and 3 to 4 metres deep in the middle, that flows out into the Bugang River. Float on a tube, jump in, or just sit by the water under the big trees. It's run as a resort with cottages along the bank, and it's an easy detour of a little over an hour if you're coming from Boracay.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season for the clearest blue; weekdays are calmer.

places.name: Manila Cathedral
places.description: Destroyed and rebuilt again and again, Manila Cathedral is the comeback story of Intramuros! Facing Plaza Roma, the Minor Basilica and Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception has survived fires, earthquakes and war. Step inside for the glowing stained-glass windows and the massive pipe organ. It's an active church, so visit outside Mass and wedding times, dress modestly and keep it quiet. Late afternoon light makes the best facade photos; then walk to San Agustin Church and Fort Santiago nearby.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings or late afternoon, outside Mass and wedding schedules

places.name: Manila Ocean Park
places.description: Want to walk under the sea without getting wet? Manila Ocean Park, right behind the Quirino Grandstand in Luneta, has been the go-to family day out since 2008. The star is the Oceanarium: a 25-meter curved glass tunnel where sharks, rays and schools of fish swim over your head, from around 277 Southeast Asian species. Add the penguins at Trails to Antarctica, the Sea Lion Show and All Star Bird Show, plus the World of Creepy Crawlies for brave kids. Pick a ticket bundle that covers what your group really wants, then time your visit around the 12:30 PM or 4:30 PM shows. Weekday mornings are the most relaxed.

places.name: Maniwaya Island and Palad Sandbar
places.description: This is Marinduque's island getaway, and the Palad Sandbar is the star! Maniwaya has a long stretch of white sand, and a short boat hop away the Palad Sandbar rises out of the sea at low tide like a floating white strip, with Ungab rock formations nearby. Swim, snorkel, camp, and watch the sun come up over the water. Visitors say the sandbar is magical when it is empty, so go on an early weekday and check the tide table first. Tip: Maniwaya is far from the main town, so stay at least one night, and book your boat and a place to sleep before you arrive.
places.best_time_to_visit: November to June; go early on a weekday and time your visit for low tide to see the Palad Sandbar.

places.name: Manjuyod Sandbar and Bais Dolphin Watching
places.description: A white strip of sand rising from the sea! The Manjuyod Sandbar appears at low tide off Bais, with stilt cottages standing over the shallow water. Boat tours from Bais start with dolphin watching in the bay, then drop you on the sandbar to wade, swim and picnic. Plan around the tide: at high tide the sand disappears under the sea. Split the boat rental with friends to make it great value, and bring snacks, water and plenty of sunscreen, since shade is scarce.
places.best_time_to_visit: Low tide on a calm, sunny day; mornings for dolphins

places.name: Mantayupan Falls
places.description: Big-waterfall drama without a long trek! Mantayupan Falls in Barili, known locally as Ambakan, is often called the tallest waterfall in Cebu, and it plunges into a cool blue-green pool wrapped in jungle. A short walk and a hanging bridge from the entrance take you right to it. Come in the rainy months for the strongest flow, then pair it with Aloguinsan's Bojo River or keep driving south to Moalboal.
places.best_time_to_visit: Rainy months give the strongest flow; late dry season, like April, can be thinner, as Reddit travellers note.

places.name: Mantigue Island
places.description: Tree-shaded white sand, clear water and some of Camiguin's best snorkeling: Mantigue is the island to pick if White Island's open sun sounds like too much! The small islet lies off Mahinog and is protected as a natural park. Snorkel over coral gardens full of fish, with a chance of spotting sea turtles, then picnic under the trees. Bring your own food and water, and go in the morning when the sea is calmest and the water clearest.
places.best_time_to_visit: Morning, dry season

places.name: Manuel Uy Beach
places.description: Pitch a tent under the trees and watch one of the best sunsets in Luzon! Manuel Uy Beach is a simple, camping-only beach on the western tip of the Calatagan peninsula in Batangas. There are no cottages and no fancy resort, just long, shallow cream-sand shores, free grilling stations and golden sunsets. Bring your own tent and food or rent gear on site, then go island hopping to Starfish Island and the sandbar by day. It is cheap, laid-back and great for a group camping weekend!
places.best_time_to_visit: Late October to May for calm water and clear skies; stay for the sunset.

places.name: Mapita View Deck and Daang Katutubo
places.description: Rolling green hills as far as you can see! Daang Katutubo is a scenic 24-kilometer road that winds across the hills of Aguilar, built to help indigenous communities reach the town proper, and it leads up to the Mapita View Deck. Drive uphill for 20 to 30 minutes, then take a short walk up for a 360-degree view of the fields, the mountains and Aguilar town below. Go on a clear morning when the hills are at their greenest!
places.best_time_to_visit: Clear, dry mornings; the hills are greenest after the first rains of the wet season.

places.name: Maquinit Hot Spring
places.description: A hot spring right by the sea! At Maquinit, warm spring water flows through stone pools that step down toward the sea and the mangroves. The hottest pools are at the top and get cooler as the water flows down, so you can pick your level of warm. It's the perfect treat for legs tired from Mt. Tapyas or a long day of island hopping. Facilities are simple, and that's part of the charm. Go after dark, when the air is cool, the stars are out and the warm water feels best.
places.best_time_to_visit: Evening, after your day's activities

places.name: Mararison Island
places.description: Grassy hills, a white sandbar and the mountains of mainland Antique as your backdrop, all on one small island! Mararison, also spelled Malalison, sits a short bangka ride off Culasi in northern Antique. Hike the ridges for a sweeping view of the coast, then cool off on the sandbar. Register at the Culasi Tourism Office before you cross, and stay overnight so you catch the sunset and the stars too.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season with calm seas; stay overnight for sunset on the ridge.

places.name: Maribina Falls
places.description: Catanduanes' easiest waterfall swim, just minutes from Virac! Maribina Falls tumbles down in a series of cascades into clear, cold pools, just right for a dip after a morning at Binurong Point or Bato Church. The name blends the two barangays it sits between, Marinawa and Binanwahan. You can drive right up and park on site, so it is an easy stop even with kids in tow. Bring a change of clothes, find a flat rock by the pools and let the cascades cool you down!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry, sunny days; skip it during or right after heavy rain, when the water runs strong.

places.name: Marlboro Country (Racuh a Payaman)
places.description: This is the Batanes postcard! Racuh a Payaman, nicknamed Marlboro Country, is a communal pasture of rolling green hills where cows, carabaos and horses graze above cliffs that drop straight into the Pacific. Tayid Lighthouse stands on a nearby hill, so you get pasture, sea and lighthouse in one frame. Walk the narrow foot trails for different angles and stay on the paths, because the animals are not pets. It's a stop on every South Batan tour, paired with Tayid Lighthouse and the Honesty Coffee Shop in Ivana. Come early morning or late afternoon for soft light, wear shoes with good grip and a windbreaker, and bring water and snacks: there are no food stalls up here.
places.best_time_to_visit: December to May (dry season); January-February is coolest. Early morning or late afternoon for light. Avoid the August-September typhoon peak.

places.name: Marlboro Hills and Blue Soil
places.description: Sagada's favorite sunrise hike! Start in the dark around 4 AM, climb through cool pine forest and reach the grassy top of Marlboro Hills (locally called Lamagan) just in time for sunrise, with a real chance of a sea of clouds rolling over the Cordillera. Grab hot black rice champorado from the hilltop stalls, then continue mostly downhill past limestone rock fields to Blue Soil (Kaman Utek), a striking slope of blue-grey earth that looks unreal in photos. It is an easy, beginner-friendly trek, about 4 to 5 hours including rest stops. A licensed local guide is required, so register at the Tourist Information Office and book your guide and shuttle the day before. Bring a flashlight, a warm jacket and shoes with good grip!
places.best_time_to_visit: Cool, dry months (roughly November to April) for clearer skies; start the trek around 4 AM to catch sunrise. The sea of clouds is never guaranteed.

places.name: Masangret Cove and Bangol Crags
places.description: Pangasinan's hidden lagoon! Masangret Cove is a small pocket of turquoise water ringed by dark rock, with a strip of soft sand and tide pools to explore, and the wide, wild beach at Bangol Crags is just along the same coast. There are no resorts, no stalls and no lifeguards, so it feels like your own secret spot. Pack food and water, come on a sunny morning and leave nothing behind!
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season, March to May, on a sunny weekday morning; skip it in the rainy months when the road turns to mud.

places.name: Masasa Beach
places.description: A budget island escape near Manila! Masasa Beach on Maricaban Island in Tingloy, Batangas has a long, pale cream shoreline, turquoise water and rock formations, with coral and fish just steps from shore. Getting there is part of the adventure: a public boat from Anilao port, then a tricycle across the island. Facilities are simple, with camping spots and homestays, keeping the vibe relaxed and group-friendly. Snorkel, swim in the small Blue Lagoon among the rocks, then camp under the stars. Go on a calm summer morning, when the water is clearest.
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May for calm seas; weekdays to avoid long boat lines

places.name: Masungi Georeserve
places.description: Like a jungle gym for grown-ups, deep in the forest! Masungi Georeserve in Baras, Rizal is a conservation area on a limestone karst ridge, where guided trails cross rope bridges, hanging walkways and the famous giant web-like Sapot net, with viewing decks over jagged rock peaks and rainforest. Visits are by reservation only, in small guided groups, so it stays calm and protected. Besides the trails, Masungi runs birding workshops and night programs like Celestial Nights. Every visit helps fund reforestation of the area. Book an early morning trail slot in the dry season, when the karst views are clearest.
places.best_time_to_visit: Dry season mornings; book weeks ahead for weekends

places.name: Mayoyao Rice Terraces
places.description: Stone-walled terraces around the town center, with native huts perched in the middle of the paddies! Mayoyao is one of the five Ifugao rice terrace clusters on the UNESCO World Heritage list, and it's far enough off the Banaue trail that it still feels like a secret. Look out for the traditional Ifugao houses on four wooden posts, with the rice granary tucked into the roof, and ask about Mayoyao's heirloom rice, passed down through generations. Golden late-afternoon light makes the stone walls glow, so stay the night if you can. It's a long ride, so start early and pack snacks!
places.best_time_to_visit: April to May for green terraces; July to August for harvest gold. Late afternoon for golden light on the walls.

places.name: Metropolitan Theater
places.description: Manila's Art Deco queen is back, and she's gorgeous! The Metropolitan Theater, or MET, was designed by Juan Arellano and inaugurated in 1931, with tropical Filipino motifs in its reliefs and a stained-glass marquee. Partly destroyed in World War II and closed in 1996, it reopened in 2021 after a grand restoration. The best way to see the inside is to catch a show, concert or ballet: a fancy but affordable date idea. Even without a ticket, the facade by Liwasang Bonifacio is a great photo stop, especially in the late afternoon.
places.best_time_to_visit: Late afternoon for facade photos; evenings for shows
